text: High voltage live parts shall comply with paragraphs 5.1.1.1. and 5.1.1.2. for protection against direct contact.
Electrical protection barriers, enclosures, solid insulators and connectors shall not be able to be opened, separated, disassembled or removed without the use of tools.

For vehicles of categories N2, N3, M2, M3, O3 and O4, electrical protection barriers, enclosures, solid insulators and connectors shall not be able to be opened, separated, disassembled or removed without the use of tools or an operator controlled activation/deactivation device or equivalent.
Connectors (including the vehicle inlet) may be separated without the use of tools only if, when separated, they comply with paragraphs 5.1.1.1. and 5.1.1.2.
condition: if the connector can be separated without tools and option (a) is used

text: Connectors (including the vehicle inlet) may be separated without the use of tools if they are provided with a locking mechanism requiring at least two distinct actions to separate the connector from its mating component, and other components not being part of the connector shall be removable only with the use of tools (or, for N2, N3, M2, M3, O3 and O4, an operator controlled activation/deactivation device or equivalent) in order to be able to separate the connector.
condition: if the connector can be separated without tools and option (b) is used

text: Connectors (including the vehicle inlet) may be separated without the use of tools if the voltage of the live parts becomes equal or below 60 V DC or equal or below 30 V AC (rms) within 1 s after the connector is separated.
condition: if the connector can be separated without tools and option (c) is used

text: Conductive connection devices not energized except during charging of the REESS are exempted from the direct contact requirement only if located on the roof of the vehicle out of reach for a person standing outside of the vehicle.
condition: if the exemption for roof-mounted conductive connection devices is used
applies_to: coupling system for charging the reess

text: For vehicles of category M2 and M3, the minimum wrap around distance from the instep of the vehicle (bottom most step at entry in case of multiple steps) to the roof mounted charging devices shall be 3 m for the exemption to apply.
condition: if the exemption for roof-mounted conductive connection devices is used
applies_to: coupling system for charging the reess

text: For high voltage live parts inside the passenger compartment, luggage compartment or trailer load compartment, the protection degree IPXXD shall be provided.
condition: high voltage live parts inside passenger, luggage or trailer load compartment

text: For high voltage live parts in areas other than the passenger compartment, luggage compartment or trailer load compartment, the protection degree IPXXB shall be provided.
condition: high voltage live parts outside passenger, luggage or trailer load compartment

text: For a high voltage service disconnect which can be opened, disassembled or removed without tools (or, for N2, N3, M2, M3, O3 and O4, with an operator controlled activation/deactivation device or equivalent), protection degree IPXXB shall be satisfied when it is opened, disassembled or removed.
condition: if the service disconnect can be opened, disassembled or removed without tools or with an operator controlled device

text: The high voltage symbol shown in Figure 2 shall be present on or near the REESS having high voltage capability, including a REESS which is part of a galvanically connected electrical circuit where the specific voltage condition is not fulfilled, independent of the maximum voltage of the REESS.
The high voltage symbol background shall be yellow, and the bordering and the arrow shall be black.

The high voltage symbol shall be visible on enclosures and electrical protection barriers which, when removed, expose live parts of high voltage circuits, except where they cannot be physically accessed, opened or removed unless other vehicle components are removed with tools, where they are located underneath the vehicle floor, or for conductive connection devices of N2, N3, M2, M3, O3 and O4 satisfying paragraph 5.1.1.; marking is optional for connectors for high voltage buses.
condition: enclosures and barriers which, when removed, expose high voltage live parts

text: Cables for high voltage buses which are not located within enclosures shall be identified by having an outer covering with the colour orange.
condition: cables not located within enclosures

text: Exposed conductive parts, such as the conductive electrical protection barrier and enclosure, shall be galvanically connected securely to the electrical chassis by electrical wire or ground cable, welding, bolts, etc. so that no dangerous potentials are produced.
The resistance between all exposed conductive parts and the electrical chassis shall be lower than 0.1 ohm when there is current flow of at least 0.2 amperes.
The resistance between any two simultaneously reachable exposed conductive parts of the electrical protection barriers that are less than 2.5 m from each other shall not exceed 0.2 Ω.

In case of doubt or if the galvanic connection is established by other means than welding, the potential equalization resistance shall be measured using one of the test procedures described in Annex 4.
condition: in case of doubt or connection not established by welding

text: Vehicles intended to be connected to the grounded external electric power supply through conductive connection between vehicle inlet and vehicle connector shall be provided with a device to enable the galvanic connection of the electrical chassis to the earth ground for the external electric power supply.
condition: vehicles charging from a stationary charging point with a charging cable of finite length through a vehicle coupler
applies_to: coupling system for charging the reess

text: The earth ground connection device should enable connection to the earth ground before exterior voltage is applied to the vehicle and retain the connection until after the exterior voltage is removed from the vehicle.
condition: vehicles charging from a stationary charging point with a charging cable of finite length through a vehicle coupler
applies_to: coupling system for charging the reess

text: If AC and DC high voltage buses are galvanically isolated from each other, isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall have a minimum value of 100 Ω/volt of the working voltage for DC buses.
condition: AC and DC buses galvanically isolated; not for circuits whose DC part is connected to chassis and specific voltage condition is fulfilled

text: If AC and DC high voltage buses are galvanically isolated from each other, isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall have a minimum value of 500 Ω/volt of the working voltage for AC buses.
condition: AC and DC buses galvanically isolated; not for circuits whose DC part is connected to chassis and specific voltage condition is fulfilled

text: The isolation resistance measurement shall be conducted according to Annex 5A.

If AC and DC high voltage buses are galvanically connected, isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall have a minimum value of 500 Ω/volt of the working voltage.
condition: AC and DC buses galvanically connected

text: If AC and DC high voltage buses are galvanically connected and all AC high voltage buses are protected by at least two layers of solid insulators, electrical protection barriers or enclosures each meeting paragraph 5.1.1. independently, or by mechanically robust protections with sufficient durability over vehicle service life, isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall have a minimum value of 100 Ω/V of the working voltage.
condition: AC and DC buses galvanically connected and all AC buses protected by measure (a) or (b)

text: Isolation resistance may be demonstrated by calculation, measurement or a combination of both; measurement shall be conducted according to Annex 5A.

In fuel cell vehicles, DC high voltage buses shall have an on-board isolation resistance monitoring system together with a warning to the driver if the isolation resistance drops below the minimum required value of 100 Ω/V.
condition: fuel cell vehicles

text: The function of the on-board isolation resistance monitoring system shall be confirmed as described in Annex 6.
condition: fuel cell vehicles

text: For the vehicle conductive connection device intended to be connected to the grounded external AC power supply and the circuit galvanically connected to it during charging, the isolation resistance between the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall comply with paragraph 5.1.3.1. when the conductive connection is disconnected, measured at the high voltage live parts (contacts) of the vehicle conductive connection device.
condition: vehicle conductive connection device for grounded external AC power supply
applies_to: coupling system for charging the reess

text: The vehicles shall maintain isolation resistance after exposure to water (e.g. washing, driving through standing water).
condition: not for circuits whose DC part is connected to chassis and specific voltage condition is fulfilled

text: The vehicle manufacturer shall provide evidence and/or documentation on how the electrical design or components located outside the passenger compartment or externally attached remain safe after water exposure and comply with Annex 7A; if not satisfactory, the manufacturer shall perform a physical component test based on Annex 7A.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses option 5.1.4.2

text: Just after each exposure of the Annex 7B test procedures, with the vehicle still wet, the vehicle shall comply with the isolation resistance test of Annex 5A and the isolation resistance requirements of paragraph 5.1.3.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses option 5.1.4.3

text: After a 24 hour pause following the Annex 7B water exposure, the isolation resistance test of Annex 5A shall again be performed and the isolation resistance requirements of paragraph 5.1.3. shall be met.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses option 5.1.4.3

text: If an isolation resistance monitoring system is provided and isolation resistance less than the requirements of paragraph 5.1.3. is detected, a warning shall be indicated to the driver.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses option 5.1.4.4

text: The function of the on-board isolation resistance monitoring system shall be confirmed as described in Annex 6.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses option 5.1.4.4

text: The REESS including related vehicle components, systems and structure as applicable shall comply with the respective requirements of paragraph 6.
condition: vehicles with REESS

text: The type of REESS shall be fully compatible with the design of the type(s) of vehicle(s).
Smoke caused by thermal propagation shall not be released into the passenger compartment, verified by design review of the intended venting strategy of the REESS and its installation.
Places for containing open type traction batteries that may produce hydrogen gas shall be provided with a ventilation fan or a ventilation duct to prevent the accumulation of hydrogen gas.
condition: vehicles with open type traction batteries

text: The vehicle shall provide a warning to the driver when the vehicle is in active driving possible mode in the event specified in paragraphs 6.13. to 6.15.

In case of optical warning of REESS failure, the tell-tale shall, when illuminated, be sufficiently bright to be visible to the driver under both daylight and night-time driving conditions when the driver has adapted to the ambient roadway light conditions.
condition: in case of optical warning

text: The REESS failure tell-tale shall be activated as a check of lamp function either when the propulsion system is turned to the "On" position or when it is in a manufacturer-designated check position between "On" and "Start"; this does not apply to tell-tales or text shown in a common space.
condition: in case of optical warning not shown in a common space

text: For vehicles of category O, the trailer shall provide an optical and/or audible warning to the driver of the towing vehicle in the event specified in paragraphs 6.13. to 6.15.; for O3 and O4 the trailer may instead provide a signal to the towing vehicle (e.g. via CAN-Bus according to ISO 11992-2).

For pure electric vehicles, a warning to the driver in the event of low REESS state of charge shall be provided, at a level of remaining REESS energy determined by the manufacturer based on engineering judgment.
condition: pure electric vehicles; not required for category O

text: In case of optical low state of charge warning, the tell-tale shall, when illuminated, be sufficiently bright to be visible to the driver under both daylight and night-time driving conditions.
condition: pure electric vehicles with optical warning

text: At least a momentary indication shall be given to the driver each time the vehicle is first placed in active driving possible mode after manual activation of the propulsion system.
condition: optional where an internal combustion engine provides propulsion power upon start up and for category O

text: For vehicles of category O, the propulsion system shall only be activated if the trailer is coupled to a towing vehicle and a signal, command or action is transmitted to the trailer propulsion system.
When leaving the vehicle, the driver shall be informed by a signal (e.g. optical or audible) if the vehicle is still in the active driving possible mode.
condition: optional where an internal combustion engine provides propulsion power while leaving and for category O

text: For vehicles of category M2 and M3 with a capacity of more than 22 passengers in addition to the driver, the active driving possible mode signal shall already be given when the driver leaves the seat.
condition: capacity of more than 22 passengers in addition to the driver

text: If the REESS can be externally charged, vehicle movement by its own propulsion system shall be impossible as long as the vehicle connector is physically connected to the vehicle inlet, demonstrated using the vehicle connector specified by the manufacturer.
condition: externally chargeable REESS, charging from a stationary charging point with a cable of finite length through a vehicle coupler

text: For vehicles of category O, a trailer parking brake shall be automatically activated as long as the trailer connector is physically connected to the trailer inlet.
condition: charging from a stationary charging point with a cable of finite length through a vehicle coupler

text: The state of the drive direction control unit shall be identified to the driver.
The hydrogen emission test shall be carried out on all vehicles equipped with open type traction batteries, unless the REESS has been approved under Part II and installed accordingly.
condition: vehicles equipped with open type traction batteries

text: The hydrogen emission test shall be conducted following the method of Annex 8 with the prescribed hydrogen sampling and analysis; other analysis methods may be approved if proven equivalent.
condition: vehicles equipped with open type traction batteries

text: During a normal charge procedure in the conditions given in Annex 8, hydrogen emissions shall be below 125 g during 5 h, or below 25 x t2 g during t2 (in h).
condition: vehicles equipped with open type traction batteries

text: During a charge carried out by a charger presenting a failure (conditions given in Annex 8), hydrogen emissions shall be below 42 g.
condition: vehicles equipped with open type traction batteries

text: The charger shall limit a possible charger failure to 30 minutes.
condition: vehicles equipped with open type traction batteries

text: All operations linked to the REESS charging, including the stop for charging, shall be controlled automatically.
condition: vehicles equipped with open type traction batteries

text: It shall not be possible to take a manual control of the charging phases.
condition: vehicles equipped with open type traction batteries

text: Normal operations of connection and disconnection to the mains or power cuts shall not affect the control system of the charging phases.
condition: vehicles equipped with open type traction batteries

text: Important charging failures (failures that can lead to a malfunction of the charger during charging later on) shall be permanently indicated.
condition: vehicles equipped with open type traction batteries

text: The manufacturer shall indicate in the owner's manual the conformity of the vehicle to the hydrogen emission requirements.
condition: vehicles equipped with open type traction batteries

text: Extension of a hydrogen emission approval to different vehicle types is permitted only for vehicle types belonging to the same family as defined in Annex 8, Appendix 2.
condition: extension of approval

text: On vehicles of categories M2/N2 and M3/N3 equipped with a high voltage electric powertrain, labels shall be installed as specified in Annex 10 (deemed satisfied if paragraph 7.1.7. of UN Regulation No. 134 is satisfied).
condition: equipped with a high voltage electric powertrain

text: For hybrid electric vehicles running on diesel or gasoline, the identification label shall indicate the high voltage powertrain as the first energy source, independent of the capacity of the REESS.
condition: hybrid electric vehicles running on diesel or gasoline

text: Identification labels shall be placed on the front of the vehicle and on the left and right sides of the vehicle, on the sides in the vicinity of a front door if available, otherwise on the first third of the vehicle length.
condition: equipped with a high voltage electric powertrain

text: For vehicles of category M2 and M3, an identification label shall additionally be fixed to the rear of the vehicle.
condition: equipped with a high voltage electric powertrain

text: The REESS test procedures prescribed in Annex 9 of this Regulation shall be applied for the Part II safety tests.
The REESS vibration test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9A to this Regulation.
During the vibration test there shall be no evidence of electrolyte leakage from the Tested-Device.
During the vibration test there shall be no evidence of rupture of the Tested-Device.
condition: high voltage REESS only

text: During the vibration test there shall be no evidence of venting of the Tested-Device.
condition: REESS other than open-type traction battery

text: During the vibration test there shall be no evidence of fire.
During the vibration test there shall be no evidence of explosion.
The evidence of electrolyte leakage in the vibration test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
An appropriate technique shall, if necessary, be used to confirm if there is any electrolyte leakage from the REESS resulting from the vibration test.
condition: if necessary

text: The evidence of venting in the vibration test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
For a high voltage REESS, the isolation resistance measured after the vibration test in accordance with Annex 5B shall not be less than 100 Ω/Volt.
condition: high voltage REESS

text: The REESS thermal shock and cycling test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9B to this Regulation.
During the thermal shock and cycling test there shall be no evidence of electrolyte leakage from the Tested-Device.
During the thermal shock and cycling test there shall be no evidence of rupture of the Tested-Device.
condition: high voltage REESS only

text: During the thermal shock and cycling test there shall be no evidence of venting of the Tested-Device.
condition: REESS other than open-type traction battery

text: During the thermal shock and cycling test there shall be no evidence of fire.
During the thermal shock and cycling test there shall be no evidence of explosion.
The evidence of electrolyte leakage in the thermal shock and cycling test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
An appropriate technique shall, if necessary, be used to confirm if there is any electrolyte leakage from the REESS resulting from the thermal shock and cycling test.
condition: if necessary

text: The evidence of venting in the thermal shock and cycling test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
For a high voltage REESS, the isolation resistance measured after the thermal shock and cycling test in accordance with Annex 5B shall not be less than 100 Ω/Volt.
condition: high voltage REESS

text: The REESS mechanical shock test may be performed, at the manufacturer's choice, as vehicle based tests per paragraph 6.4.1.1., component based tests per paragraph 6.4.1.2., or any combination of both for different directions of vehicle travel.

Compliance with the mechanical shock acceptance criteria may be demonstrated by REESS installed in vehicles subjected to crash tests per UN R94 Annex 3 or UN R137 Annex 3 for frontal impact and UN R95 Annex 4 for side impact.
condition: vehicle based mechanical shock test

text: In the vehicle based mechanical shock test, the ambient temperature and the SOC shall be in accordance with UN Regulations Nos. 94, 137 and 95 as applicable.
condition: vehicle based mechanical shock test

text: The vehicle based mechanical shock requirement is deemed to be met if the vehicle with high voltage electric power train is approved to UN R94 (04 series or later) or UN R137 (02 series or later) for frontal impact and UN R95 (05 series or later) for lateral impact.
condition: vehicle based mechanical shock test

text: The approval of a REESS tested under the vehicle based mechanical shock test shall be limited to the specific vehicle type.
condition: REESS tested per paragraph 6.4.1.1.

text: The component based mechanical shock test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9C to this Regulation.
condition: component based mechanical shock test

text: During the mechanical shock test there shall be no evidence of fire.
During the mechanical shock test there shall be no evidence of explosion.
For an aqueous electrolyte REESS, from the impact until 60 minutes after the impact there shall be no electrolyte leakage from the REESS into the passenger compartment.
condition: aqueous electrolyte REESS tested per paragraph 6.4.1.1.

text: For an aqueous electrolyte REESS, from the impact until 60 minutes after the impact no more than 7 per cent by volume of the REESS electrolyte with a maximum of 5.0 l shall leak from the REESS to the outside of the passenger compartment.
condition: aqueous electrolyte REESS tested per paragraph 6.4.1.1.

text: For containers containing Stoddard, coloured coolant and electrolyte, the fluids shall be allowed to separate by specific gravity and then measured.
condition: aqueous electrolyte REESS tested per paragraph 6.4.1.1.

text: For a non-aqueous electrolyte REESS, from the impact until 60 minutes after the impact there shall be no liquid electrolyte leakage from the REESS into the passenger compartment or luggage compartment and no liquid electrolyte leakage to outside the vehicle.
condition: non-aqueous electrolyte REESS tested per paragraph 6.4.1.1.

text: The non-aqueous electrolyte leakage requirement shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the vehicle.
condition: non-aqueous electrolyte REESS tested per paragraph 6.4.1.1.

text: After the vehicle based test, the REESS shall remain attached to the vehicle by at least one component anchorage, bracket, or any structure that transfers loads from REESS to the vehicle structure.
condition: tested per paragraph 6.4.1.1.

text: After the vehicle based test, a REESS located outside the passenger compartment shall not enter the passenger compartment.
condition: tested per paragraph 6.4.1.1.; REESS located outside the passenger compartment

text: After the component based mechanical shock test, the Tested-Device shall be retained by its mounting and its components shall remain inside its boundaries.
condition: tested per paragraph 6.4.1.2.

text: For a high voltage REESS, the isolation resistance of the Tested-Device shall ensure at least 100 Ω/Volt for the whole REESS measured after the mechanical shock test in accordance with Annex 5A or Annex 5B, or the protection degree IPXXB shall be fulfilled for the Tested-Device.
condition: high voltage REESS

text: For a REESS tested in accordance with paragraph 6.4.1.2., the evidence of electrolyte leakage shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
condition: tested per paragraph 6.4.1.2.

text: The mechanical integrity test applies only to a REESS intended for installation in vehicles of categories M1 and N1, and may be performed at the manufacturer's choice as vehicle based tests per 6.4.2.1. or component based tests per 6.4.2.2.
condition: REESS intended for installation in M1 and N1 vehicles

text: The vehicle specific mechanical integrity test may be performed, at the manufacturer's choice, as a vehicle based dynamic test per 6.4.2.1.1., a vehicle specific component test per 6.4.2.1.2., or any combination for different directions of vehicle travel.
condition: vehicle specific test

text: When the REESS is mounted between a line from the rear edge of the vehicle perpendicular to the centre line of the vehicle and 300 mm forward and parallel to this line, the manufacturer shall demonstrate the mechanical integrity performance of the REESS in the vehicle to the Technical Service.
condition: REESS mounted within 300 mm forward of the vehicle rear edge

text: The approval of a REESS tested under the vehicle specific mechanical integrity test shall be limited to the specific vehicle type.
condition: REESS tested per paragraph 6.4.2.1.

text: Compliance with the mechanical integrity acceptance criteria may be demonstrated by REESS installed in vehicles subjected to a crash test per Annex 3 to UN R94 or R137 for frontal impact and Annex 4 to R95 for side impact.
condition: vehicle based dynamic test

text: In the vehicle based dynamic mechanical integrity test, the ambient temperature and the SOC shall be in accordance with the said crash Regulations.
condition: vehicle based dynamic test

text: The vehicle based dynamic mechanical integrity requirement is deemed to be met if the vehicle with high voltage electric power train is approved to UN R94 (04 series or later) or UN R137 (02 series or later) for frontal impact and UN R95 (05 series or later) for lateral impact.
condition: vehicle based dynamic test

text: The vehicle specific component mechanical integrity test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9D.
condition: vehicle specific component test

text: The crush force of Annex 9D paragraph 3.2.1. may be replaced with the value declared by the vehicle manufacturer using data from actual crash tests or simulation per Annex 3 of UN R94 or R137 in the direction of travel and Annex 4 of UN R95 horizontally perpendicular to it; these forces shall be agreed by the Technical Service.
condition: vehicle specific component test with declared crush force

text: Forces derived from alternative crash test procedures, used in agreement with the Technical Service, shall be equal to or greater than the forces resulting from data in accordance with UN R94, R137 and R95.
condition: alternative crash test procedures used

text: The vehicle specific component test shall be conducted with the REESS mounted to the vehicle structure defined by the manufacturer in a way which is representative of its mounting in the vehicle.
condition: manufacturer defines relevant vehicle structure parts

text: The component based mechanical integrity test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9D.
condition: component based test

text: A REESS approved according to the component based mechanical integrity test shall be mounted between a vertical plane perpendicular to the vehicle centre line located 420 mm rearward from the front edge of the vehicle and a vertical plane perpendicular to the centre line located 300 mm forward from the rear edge of the vehicle.
condition: REESS approved per paragraph 6.4.2.2.

text: The REESS mounting restrictions shall be documented in Annex 1 - Appendix 2.
condition: REESS approved per paragraph 6.4.2.2.

text: Where the crush force of Annex 9D paragraph 3.2.1. is replaced by a manufacturer declared value, that crush force shall be documented in Annex 1, Appendix 2 as a mounting restriction.
condition: declared crush force used

text: The vehicle manufacturer using a REESS with declared crush force shall demonstrate during Part I approval that the contact force to the REESS will not exceed the figure declared by the REESS manufacturer.
condition: declared crush force used

text: The contact force shall be determined by the vehicle manufacturer using data from actual crash test or simulation per Annex 3 to UN R94 or R137 in the direction of travel and Annex 4 to R95 horizontally perpendicular to it, and agreed together with the Technical Service.
condition: declared crush force used

text: Forces derived from alternative crash test procedures, used in agreement with the Technical Service, shall be equal to or greater than the forces resulting from data in accordance with the specified Regulations.
condition: alternative crash test procedures used

text: The fire resistance test is required for REESS containing flammable electrolyte.
condition: REESS containing flammable electrolyte

text: The fire resistance test is not required when the REESS as installed in the vehicle is mounted such that the lowest surface of its casing is more than 1.5 m above the ground; at the manufacturer's request the test may nevertheless be performed.
condition: lowest surface of REESS casing more than 1.5 m above the ground

text: The fire resistance test shall be carried out on one test sample, at the manufacturer's choice as a vehicle based test per 6.5.1. or a component based test per 6.5.2.
condition: REESS containing flammable electrolyte

text: The vehicle based fire resistance test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9E paragraph 3.2.1.
condition: vehicle based test

text: The approval of a REESS tested according to the vehicle based fire resistance test shall be limited to approvals for a specific vehicle type.
condition: vehicle based test

text: The component based fire resistance test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9E paragraph 3.2.2.
condition: component based test

text: During the fire resistance test, the tested-device shall exhibit no evidence of explosion.
The external short circuit protection test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9F.
During the external short circuit protection test there shall be no evidence of electrolyte leakage.
During the external short circuit protection test there shall be no evidence of rupture.
condition: high voltage REESS only

text: During the external short circuit protection test there shall be no evidence of venting.
condition: REESS other than open-type traction battery

text: During the external short circuit protection test there shall be no evidence of fire.
During the external short circuit protection test there shall be no evidence of explosion.
The evidence of electrolyte leakage in the external short circuit protection test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
An appropriate technique shall, if necessary, be used to confirm if there is any electrolyte leakage from the REESS resulting from the external short circuit protection test.
condition: if necessary

text: The evidence of venting in the external short circuit protection test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
For a high voltage REESS, the isolation resistance measured after the external short circuit protection test in accordance with Annex 5B shall not be less than 100 Ω/Volt.
condition: high voltage REESS

text: The overcharge protection test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9G.
During the overcharge protection test there shall be no evidence of electrolyte leakage.
During the overcharge protection test there shall be no evidence of rupture.
condition: high voltage REESS only

text: During the overcharge protection test there shall be no evidence of venting.
condition: REESS other than open-type traction battery

text: During the overcharge protection test there shall be no evidence of fire.
During the overcharge protection test there shall be no evidence of explosion.
The evidence of electrolyte leakage in the overcharge protection test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
An appropriate technique shall, if necessary, be used to confirm if there is any electrolyte leakage from the REESS resulting from the overcharge protection test.
condition: if necessary

text: The evidence of venting in the overcharge protection test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
For a high voltage REESS, the isolation resistance measured after the overcharge protection test in accordance with Annex 5B shall not be less than 100 Ω/Volt.
condition: high voltage REESS

text: The over-discharge protection test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9H.
During the over-discharge protection test there shall be no evidence of electrolyte leakage.
During the over-discharge protection test there shall be no evidence of rupture.
condition: high voltage REESS only

text: During the over-discharge protection test there shall be no evidence of venting.
condition: REESS other than open-type traction battery

text: During the over-discharge protection test there shall be no evidence of fire.
During the over-discharge protection test there shall be no evidence of explosion.
The evidence of electrolyte leakage in the over-discharge protection test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
An appropriate technique shall, if necessary, be used to confirm if there is any electrolyte leakage from the REESS resulting from the over-discharge protection test.
condition: if necessary

text: The evidence of venting in the over-discharge protection test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
For a high voltage REESS, the isolation resistance measured after the over-discharge protection test in accordance with Annex 5B shall not be less than 100 Ω/Volt.
condition: high voltage REESS

text: The over-temperature protection test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9I.
During the over-temperature protection test there shall be no evidence of electrolyte leakage.
During the over-temperature protection test there shall be no evidence of rupture.
condition: high voltage REESS only

text: During the over-temperature protection test there shall be no evidence of venting.
condition: REESS other than open-type traction battery

text: During the over-temperature protection test there shall be no evidence of fire.
During the over-temperature protection test there shall be no evidence of explosion.
The evidence of electrolyte leakage in the over-temperature protection test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
An appropriate technique shall, if necessary, be used to confirm if there is any electrolyte leakage from the REESS resulting from the over-temperature protection test.
condition: if necessary

text: The evidence of venting in the over-temperature protection test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
For a high voltage REESS, the isolation resistance measured after the over-temperature protection test in accordance with Annex 5B shall not be less than 100 Ω/Volt.
condition: high voltage REESS

text: The overcurrent protection test is required for REESS intended for use on vehicles of categories M1 and N1 that have the capability of charging by DC external electricity supply.
condition: vehicle capable of charging by DC external electricity supply

text: The overcurrent protection test shall be conducted in accordance with Annex 9J.
condition: vehicle capable of charging by DC external electricity supply

text: During the overcurrent protection test there shall be no evidence of electrolyte leakage.
condition: vehicle capable of charging by DC external electricity supply

text: During the overcurrent protection test there shall be no evidence of rupture.
condition: high voltage REESS only

text: During the overcurrent protection test there shall be no evidence of venting.
condition: REESS other than open-type traction battery

text: During the overcurrent protection test there shall be no evidence of fire.
condition: vehicle capable of charging by DC external electricity supply

text: During the overcurrent protection test there shall be no evidence of explosion.
condition: vehicle capable of charging by DC external electricity supply

text: The evidence of electrolyte leakage in the overcurrent protection test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
An appropriate technique shall, if necessary, be used to confirm if there is any electrolyte leakage from the REESS resulting from the overcurrent protection test.
condition: if necessary

text: The evidence of venting in the overcurrent protection test shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.

The overcurrent protection control of the REESS shall terminate charging, or the temperature measured on the casing of the REESS shall be stabilized such that the temperature gradient varies by less than 4 °C through 2 hours after the maximum overcurrent charging level is reached.
condition: vehicle capable of charging by DC external electricity supply

text: For a high voltage REESS, the isolation resistance measured after the overcurrent protection test in accordance with Annex 5B shall not be less than 100 Ω/V.
condition: high voltage REESS

text: The REESS manufacturer must make available, at the request of the Technical Service, a system diagram demonstrating that the REESS monitors and appropriately controls REESS operations at low temperatures at its safety boundary limits.
condition: at the request of the Technical Service

text: The REESS manufacturer must make available, at the request of the Technical Service, a written explanation on the lower boundary temperature for safe operation of the REESS.
condition: at the request of the Technical Service

text: The REESS manufacturer must make available, at the request of the Technical Service, documentation of the method of detecting REESS temperature.
condition: at the request of the Technical Service

text: The REESS manufacturer must make available, at the request of the Technical Service, documentation of the action taken when the REESS temperature is at or lower than the lower boundary for safe operation of the REESS.
condition: at the request of the Technical Service

text: Under vehicle operation including the operation with a failure, the vehicle occupants shall not be exposed to any hazardous environment caused by emissions from REESS.
applies_to: management of gases emitted from reess

text: Open-type traction batteries shall meet the requirements of paragraph 5.4. with regard to hydrogen emissions.
condition: REESS is an open-type traction battery
applies_to: management of gases emitted from reess

text: For REESS other than open-type traction battery, the requirement of paragraph 6.12.1 is deemed satisfied if all applicable requirements of the tests of paragraphs 6.2 (vibration), 6.3 (thermal shock and cycling), 6.6 (external short circuit protection), 6.7 (overcharge protection), 6.8 (over-discharge protection), 6.9 (over-temperature protection), 6.10 (overcurrent protection) and 6.15 (thermal propagation) are met.
condition: REESS other than open-type traction battery
applies_to: management of gases emitted from reess

text: The REESS or vehicle system shall provide a signal to activate the warning specified in paragraph 5.2.3 in the event of operational failure of the vehicle controls (e.g. input and output signals to the REESS management system, sensors within REESS) that manage the safe operation of the REESS.

The REESS or vehicle manufacturer shall make available, at the request of the Technical Service, documentation explaining safety performance of the system level or subsystem level of the vehicle with regard to operational failure of vehicle controls managing REESS safe operation.
condition: at the request of the Technical Service

text: The documentation shall include a system diagram identifying all the vehicle controls that manage REESS operations, identifying the components used to generate a warning due to operational failure of vehicle controls to conduct one or more basic operations.
condition: at the request of the Technical Service

text: The documentation shall include a written explanation of the basic operation of the vehicle controls that manage REESS operation, identifying the components of the vehicle control system, describing their functions and capability to manage the REESS, and providing a logic diagram and description of conditions that would lead to triggering of the warning.
condition: at the request of the Technical Service

text: The REESS or vehicle system shall provide a signal to activate the warning specified in paragraph 5.2.3 in the case of a thermal event in the REESS (as specified by the manufacturer).

The REESS or vehicle manufacturer shall make available, at the request of the Technical Service, documentation explaining safety performance of the system level or subsystem level of the vehicle with regard to thermal events in the REESS.
condition: at the request of the Technical Service

text: The documentation shall include the parameters and associated threshold levels used to indicate a thermal event (e.g. temperature, temperature rise rate, SOC level, voltage drop, electrical current) to trigger the warning.
condition: at the request of the Technical Service

text: The documentation shall include a system diagram and written explanation describing the sensors and operation of the vehicle controls to manage the REESS in the event of a thermal event.
condition: at the request of the Technical Service

text: For a REESS containing flammable electrolyte or alkali metal anodes, the vehicle occupants shall not be exposed to any hazardous environment caused by thermal propagation triggered by an internal short circuit leading to a single cell thermal runaway; the requirements of paragraphs 6.15.1 and 6.15.2 shall be satisfied in accordance with the verification procedure of paragraph 6.15.3.
condition: REESS containing flammable electrolyte or alkali metal anodes; not applicable to REESS solely installed on category O vehicles nor to batteries on category O vehicles used for recuperation only

text: The REESS or vehicle system shall provide a signal to activate the warning specified in paragraph 5.2.3 in the event of a thermal propagation triggered by an internal short circuit leading to a single cell thermal runaway in order to allow egress.
condition: REESS containing flammable electrolyte or alkali metal anodes; warning not mandatory if single cell thermal runaway does not lead to thermal propagation within 2 hours or cannot be triggered

text: The thermal propagation warning requirement is deemed met if a hazardous situation as defined in paragraph 6.15.3.4 does not occur within 5 minutes following the warning signal, or the single cell thermal runaway does not lead to thermal propagation in the REESS during 2 hours after its triggering, or the single cell thermal runaway cannot be triggered as confirmed by repeating the same test procedure or by a cell level test.
condition: REESS containing flammable electrolyte or alkali metal anodes

text: The REESS or vehicle manufacturer shall make available documentation of the parameters (e.g. temperature, voltage or electrical current) which trigger the thermal propagation warning indication.
condition: REESS containing flammable electrolyte or alkali metal anodes

text: The REESS or vehicle manufacturer shall make available a description of the thermal propagation warning system.
condition: REESS containing flammable electrolyte or alkali metal anodes

text: The REESS or vehicle system shall have functions or characteristics in the cell, REESS or vehicle intended to protect vehicle occupants in conditions caused by thermal propagation triggered by an internal short circuit leading to a single cell thermal runaway.
condition: REESS containing flammable electrolyte or alkali metal anodes

text: Conformance with thermal propagation safety shall be demonstrated by physical testing according to Annex 9K or, where physical testing is not possible without compromising the REESS safety design, by a systematic risk management analysis according to paragraph 6.15.4.
condition: REESS containing flammable electrolyte or alkali metal anodes

text: The Type Approval Authority and the Technical Service shall determine, with the help of documentation provided by the manufacturer, whether physical testing is possible without compromising the safety functionality and design of the vehicle and/or REESS.

If the REESS is designed to be charged only by an energy source on the vehicle and its capacity in Ah multiplied by its nominal voltage does not exceed 2 kWh, only the risk management analysis according to paragraph 6.15.4 needs to be performed.
condition: REESS charged only by on-vehicle energy source and capacity x nominal voltage ≤ 2 kWh

text: The manufacturer shall provide technical documentation containing a system diagram of all relevant physical systems and components.
The manufacturer shall provide a diagram showing the functional operation of the relevant systems and components, identifying all risk mitigation functions or characteristics.
For each identified risk mitigation function or characteristic implemented, the physical system or component which implements the function shall be identified and the operating strategy described.
The manufacturer's technical documentation shall state the maximum operating temperature.
The manufacturer's technical documentation shall contain recommendations on the feasibility for conducting the physical testing.

The manufacturer's technical documentation shall contain recommendations on a more suitable and feasible trigger method including appropriate parameters, the preparation and instrumentation of the Tested-Device.
condition: if applicable

text: The manufacturer's technical documentation shall contain recommendations on pre-instrumentation of the triggering and measuring devices including sufficient details of such pre-instrumentation.
condition: if applicable

text: The Technical Service shall start the selection of the trigger method for physical thermal propagation testing by considering localized fast external heating first; alternative methods (localized internal heater, nail penetration, laser-based trigger) may be used only if recommended by the manufacturer and recognized by the Technical Service as more suitable to cause single cell thermal runaway satisfying Annex 9K paragraph 5.
The decision of the Technical Service on the trigger method shall be duly documented and justified in the test report.
Either the vehicle-based test or the component-based thermal propagation test shall be performed.

The vehicle-based thermal propagation test shall be carried out if the REESS casing lacks an intended venting system and smoke due to thermal propagation occurs during the test, or if this smoke is released from locations other than the intended venting system.
condition: REESS lacks intended venting system and smoke occurs, or smoke released from other locations

text: It shall be demonstrated that the component-based thermal propagation test is representative of vehicle-level behaviour.
condition: component-based test is used

text: Vehicle parts which may affect the outcome of the thermal propagation test (e.g. due to essential deformation) shall be included in the test set-up in agreement with the Technical Service and Type Approval Authority.
condition: vehicle parts may affect the test outcome

text: In case of doubt, the thermal propagation test shall be performed at vehicle level or shall at least include the parts of the vehicle relevant for the test.
condition: in case of doubt

text: For 5 minutes following the signal to activate the warning indication, no fire caused by thermal propagation shall occur.
For 5 minutes following the signal to activate the warning indication, no explosion caused by thermal propagation shall occur.
For 5 minutes following the signal to activate the warning indication, no smoke release into the passenger compartment caused by thermal propagation shall occur.

The warning indicator may occur either when the triggered cell enters thermal runaway or when the REESS has reliably identified a thermal propagation event, provided that the safety objectives are met.

For the vehicle-based test, evidence of fire, explosion and smoke release into the passenger compartment shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device or vehicle.
condition: vehicle-based test

text: For the component-based test, evidence of fire, explosion and smoke from thermal propagation not escaping the REESS through the intended venting system shall be verified by visual inspection without disassembling any part of the Tested-Device.
condition: component-based test

text: If no thermal propagation is observed during the 2 hours after thermal runaway was triggered in the initiation cell, the requirements of paragraph 6.15.3.4 are deemed satisfied.
condition: no thermal propagation within 2 hours

text: If thermal runaway is not triggered with the chosen trigger method, and this is confirmed by repetition of the same test procedure or by a cell level test with the same trigger method, the requirements of paragraph 6.15.3.4 are deemed satisfied.
condition: thermal runaway not triggered and confirmed

text: The manufacturer shall perform and document a holistic, systematic risk assessment including hardware and software aspects to consider occupant protection in normal operating conditions, explaining the safety performance of the vehicle systems in conditions caused by thermal propagation triggered by an internal short circuit leading to a single cell thermal runaway.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required following paragraph 6.15.3

text: The manufacturer shall make available to the Type Approval Authority and Technical Service a high-level report including essential data and a summary on occupant protection in case of single cell thermal runaway and thermal propagation, comprising four parts relating to paragraphs 6.15.4.1 to 6.15.4.4.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The Type Approval Authority and/or Technical Service shall assess the risk management analysis with regard to ensuring the safety of the occupants in the event of thermal propagation.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The system analysis shall include a system diagram of all relevant physical systems and components.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The system analysis shall include a description of systems and components relevant to single-cell thermal runaway and thermal propagation due to internal short circuit and their interoperability (e.g. REESS, sensors, thermal management system, battery management systems).
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The system analysis shall include a description of the warning indication and of its operating logic.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The system analysis shall include functional analyses identifying the conditions leading to single cell thermal runaway (internal short circuit) and allocating them to the corresponding components, functional units or subsystems.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: A risk identification and mitigation analysis using appropriate industry standard methodology shall document the hazards to vehicle occupants caused by thermal propagation triggered by an internal short circuit leading to single cell thermal runaway, and the risk reduction from the identified risk mitigation functions or characteristics.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The severity of the thermal event and the risk of propagation to adjacent cells in the battery pack shall be determined.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The risk identification and mitigation analysis shall include, as appropriate, risk mitigation by design, by manufacturing control and by other means.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The risk analysis shall include information and justifications about any assumptions on system performance characteristics and properties, model behaviour or relative relevance and the likelihood of specified risk scenarios.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The effectiveness of each of the risk reduction measures shall be analysed and evaluated, fulfilling paragraphs 6.15.4.3.1 and 6.15.4.3.2 as appropriate.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: Test and verification methods used for unit testing, implementation testing and validation shall be documented, clearly identifying which safety functionalities are addressed with the respective methods.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: In the absence of appropriate industry standard methods and tests, the manufacturer shall design feasible test methods and verification techniques to verify and validate the effectiveness of the risk mitigation strategy, explicitly documented including what is tested, the suitability of the method and the rationale.
condition: absence of appropriate industry standard methods

text: The data set shall evaluate performance of the components and functional units identified in the allocation process; the relevance and appropriateness of the data shall be described and justified.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: Major uncertainty factors shall be identified and quantified as far as possible.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: All relevant results available shall be gathered to create a full consistent report, and the sources of externally derived data shall be identified.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: A completeness check shall be conducted to ensure all relevant information and data needed for interpretation are available and complete.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: A sensitivity check shall be conducted to evaluate the reliability of the final results and conclusions with regard to uncertainties in data, allocation methods or assumptions about the REESS.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The concluding part of the report shall comprise a brief summary of the major results of the risk management analysis and a statement that the requirements of paragraphs 6.15.1 and 6.15.2 are satisfied, including that the methods used are scientifically and technically valid for the scope of the analysis.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The conclusions shall state that the data used are appropriate and reasonable in relation to the intention of the risk management analysis.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: The conclusions shall state that the interpretations are relevant and reflect the assumptions made and the limitations identified for the study.
condition: if risk management analysis is applicable/required

text: REESS and vehicle shall be compatible with regard to their communication.

For a REESS type approved in accordance with Part II, installation shall be in accordance with the instructions provided by the REESS manufacturer and in conformity with the description in Annex 1, Part 2.
condition: REESS type approved under Part II installed for vehicle approval under Part III

text: For vehicle approval under Part III, the requirements of paragraphs 5.1 to 5.1.4.4 and 5.2.2 to 5.5.3 shall be met.
condition: vehicle approval under Part III

text: The conformity of production procedure shall comply with the requirements set out in Schedule 1 of the Agreement (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3).
Vehicles or REESS approved under this Regulation shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements of the relevant part(s) of this Regulation.
Appropriate production checks shall be carried out to verify that the requirements of paragraph 9.1 are met.

The communication concerning the approval, extension, refusal or withdrawal of approval or production definitively discontinued of a REESS type as component/separate technical unit shall follow the model of Annex 1 - Part 2, with a maximum format of A4 (210 x 297 mm).
The REESS approval communication shall state the installation restrictions applicable to the REESS as described in paragraphs 6.4., 6.5., 6.10., 6.15. and 6.16.
The REESS approval communication shall state the intended category of vehicles for installing the REESS.
The information document on essential characteristics of the vehicle shall give the type of fuse and/or circuit breaker.
The information document shall give a diagram showing the functional range of the fuse and/or circuit breaker.
The information document on essential characteristics of the vehicle shall give the type of power wiring harness.
The information document on essential characteristics of the vehicle shall give a description of the protection concept against electric shock.
The approval mark shall be arranged in accordance with the models of Annex 2, with the dimension a of at least 8 mm.
The approval mark affixed to a REESS shall include the symbol "ES" following the "R" as shown in Figure 2 of Annex 2.
condition: in the case of approval of a REESS

text: The protection of persons against access to live parts shall be verified using the access probes given in Table 1 of Annex 3.

The access probe shall be pushed against any openings of the enclosure with the force specified in Table 1 and, if it partly or fully penetrates, placed in every possible position, but in no case shall the stop face fully penetrate through the opening.
Internal electrical protection barriers shall be considered part of the enclosure during the access probe test.

If necessary, a low-voltage supply of not less than 40 V and not more than 50 V in series with a suitable lamp should be connected between the probe and live parts inside the electrical protection barrier or enclosure, and the signal-circuit method should also be applied to moving live parts of high voltage equipment.
condition: if necessary

text: The access probe shall not touch live parts; if verified by a signal circuit between the probe and live parts, the lamp shall not light.
In the test for protection degree IPXXB, the jointed test finger may penetrate to its 80 mm length, but the stop face (diameter 50 mm x 20 mm) shall not pass through the opening.
condition: test for protection degree IPXXB

text: In the IPXXB test, starting from the straight position, both joints of the test finger shall be successively bent through an angle of up to 90 degrees with respect to the axis of the adjoining section of the finger and shall be placed in every possible position.
condition: test for protection degree IPXXB

text: In the test for protection degree IPXXD, the access probe may penetrate to its full length, but the stop face shall not fully penetrate through the opening.
condition: test for protection degree IPXXD

text: The jointed test finger shall be of metal, except where otherwise specified, with tolerances on dimensions without specific tolerance of 0/-10 seconds on angles, 0/-0.05 mm on linear dimensions up to 25 mm and ±0.2 mm on linear dimensions over 25 mm.
Both joints of the jointed test finger shall permit movement in the same plane and the same direction through an angle of 90° with a 0 to +10° tolerance.

When verifying potential equalization with a resistance tester connected between the measuring points (typically electrical chassis and electro conductive enclosure/electrical protection barrier), the resistance tester shall have a measurement current of at least 0.2 A.
condition: test method using a resistance tester

text: The resistance tester used for verification of potential equalization shall have a resolution of 0.01 Ω or less.
condition: test method using a resistance tester

text: The resistance R measured between the electrical chassis and the electro conductive enclosure/electrical protection barrier shall be less than 0.1 Ω.
condition: test method using a resistance tester

text: In the test method using DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter connected to the measuring points, the voltage of the DC power supply shall be adjusted so that the current flow becomes at least 0.2 A, and the resistance shall be calculated as R = U / I.
condition: test method using DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter

text: The resistance R calculated with the DC power supply method between the electrical chassis and the electro conductive enclosure/electrical protection barrier shall be less than 0.1 Ω.
condition: test method using DC power supply, voltmeter and ammeter

text: If lead wires are used for voltage and current measurement, each lead wire shall be independently connected to the electrical protection barrier/enclosure/electrical chassis.
condition: if lead wires are used for voltage and current measurement

text: The isolation resistance for each high voltage bus of the vehicle shall be measured or determined by calculation using measurement values from each part or component unit of a high voltage bus (divided measurement).
condition: vehicle based tests

text: The vehicle-based isolation resistance measurement shall be conducted by selecting an appropriate method from paragraphs 2.1. through 2.2. of Annex 5A, depending on the electrical charge of the live parts or the isolation resistance; megohmmeter or oscilloscope measurements are appropriate alternatives.
The range of the electrical circuit to be measured shall be clarified in advance, using electrical circuit diagrams.
If the high voltage buses are conductively isolated from each other, isolation resistance shall be measured for each electrical circuit.
condition: if the high voltage buses are conductively isolated from each other

text: Modifications made for measuring the isolation resistance (e.g. cover removal, measurement lines, software change, stopping or removing the on-board isolation resistance monitoring system) shall not influence the test results; when the monitoring device is removed, drawings shall prove that the isolation resistance between live parts and the electrical chassis remains unchanged.
condition: if modifications are carried out for the measurement

text: Utmost care shall be exercised as to short circuit and electric shock during the isolation resistance measurement.
An isolation resistance test instrument capable of applying a DC voltage higher than the working voltage of the high voltage bus shall be used.
condition: measurement method using DC voltage from external sources

text: The isolation resistance test instrument shall be connected between the live parts and the electrical chassis and the isolation resistance shall be measured by applying a DC voltage at least half of the working voltage of the high voltage bus.
condition: measurement method using DC voltage from external sources

text: Where the system has several voltage ranges in a galvanically connected circuit and some components cannot withstand the working voltage of the entire circuit, the isolation resistance between those components and the electrical chassis may be measured separately by applying at least half of their own working voltage with those components disconnected.
condition: if some components cannot withstand the working voltage of the entire circuit

text: The high voltage bus shall be energized by the vehicle's own REESS and/or energy conversion system and the voltage level throughout the test shall be at least the nominal operating voltage as specified by the vehicle manufacturer.
condition: measurement method using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source

text: The voltmeter used in the vehicle-based isolation resistance test shall measure DC values and shall have an internal resistance of at least 10 MΩ.
condition: measurement method using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source

text: The high voltage bus voltage Ub shall be measured and recorded and shall be equal to or greater than the nominal operating voltage of the REESS and/or energy conversion system as specified by the vehicle manufacturer.
condition: measurement method using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source

text: The voltage U1 between the negative side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall be measured and recorded.
condition: measurement method using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source

text: The voltage U2 between the positive side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis shall be measured and recorded.
condition: measurement method using the vehicle's own REESS as DC voltage source

text: If U1 is greater than or equal to U2, a standard known resistance Ro shall be inserted between the negative side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis, U1' measured, and the electrical isolation calculated as Ri = Ro*Ub*(1/U1' - 1/U1).
condition: if U1 is greater than or equal to U2

text: If U2 is greater than U1, a standard known resistance Ro shall be inserted between the positive side of the high voltage bus and the electrical chassis, U2' measured, and the electrical isolation calculated as Ri = Ro*Ub*(1/U2' - 1/U2).
condition: if U2 is greater than U1

text: The isolation resistance (in Ω/V) shall be obtained by dividing the electrical isolation value Ri (in Ω) by the working voltage of the high voltage bus (in V).

The isolation resistance measurement for component based tests of a REESS shall be conducted by selecting an appropriate method from paragraphs 1.1. through 1.2. of Annex 5B, depending on the electrical charge of the live parts or the isolation resistance; megohmmeter or oscilloscope measurements are appropriate alternatives.
condition: component based tests of a REESS

text: The range of the electrical circuit to be measured shall be clarified in advance using electrical circuit diagrams, and if the high voltage buses are galvanically isolated from each other, isolation resistance shall be measured for each electrical circuit.
condition: component based tests of a REESS

text: If the operating voltage Ub of the Tested-Device cannot be measured (e.g. due to contactor or fuse operation), the test may be performed with a modified test device allowing measurement of the internal voltages upstream the main contactors.
condition: if the operating voltage of the Tested-Device cannot be measured

text: Modifications made for measuring the REESS isolation resistance shall not influence the test results; when the isolation resistance monitoring device is removed, drawings shall prove that the isolation resistance between the live parts and the manufacturer-designated ground connection remains unchanged.
condition: if modifications are carried out for the measurement

text: Utmost care shall be exercised as to short circuit and electric shock during the REESS isolation resistance measurement.
An isolation resistance test instrument capable of applying a DC voltage higher than the nominal voltage of the tested-device shall be used.
condition: measurement method using DC voltage from external sources

text: The insulation resistance test instrument shall be connected between the live parts and the ground connection of the Tested-Device and the isolation resistance shall be measured.
condition: measurement method using DC voltage from external sources

text: Where the system has several voltage ranges in a galvanically connected circuit and some components cannot withstand the working voltage of the entire circuit, the isolation resistance between those components and the ground connection may be measured separately by applying at least half of their own working voltage with those components disconnected.
condition: if some components cannot withstand the working voltage of the entire circuit

text: The voltage level of the tested-device throughout the test shall be at least the nominal operating voltage of the tested-device.
condition: measurement method using the tested-device as DC voltage source

text: The voltmeter used in the component-based isolation resistance test shall measure DC values and shall have an internal resistance of at least 10 MΩ.
condition: measurement method using the tested-device as DC voltage source

text: The operating voltage Ub of the Tested-Device shall be measured and recorded and shall be equal to or greater than the nominal operating voltage of the Tested-Device.
condition: measurement method using the tested-device as DC voltage source

text: The voltage U1 between the negative pole of the Tested-Device and the ground connection shall be measured and recorded.
condition: measurement method using the tested-device as DC voltage source

text: The voltage U2 between the positive pole of the Tested-Device and the ground connection shall be measured and recorded.
condition: measurement method using the tested-device as DC voltage source

text: If U1 is greater than or equal to U2, a standard known resistance Ro shall be inserted between the negative pole of the Tested-Device and the ground connection, U1' measured, and the electrical isolation calculated as Ri = Ro*Ub*(1/U1' - 1/U1).
condition: if U1 is greater than or equal to U2

text: If U2 is greater than U1, a standard known resistance Ro shall be inserted between the positive pole of the Tested-Device and the ground connection, U2' measured, and the electrical isolation calculated as Ri = Ro*Ub*(1/U2' - 1/U2).
condition: if U2 is greater than U1

text: The isolation resistance (in Ω/V) shall be obtained by dividing the electrical isolation value Ri (in Ω) by the nominal voltage of the Tested-Device (in V).

The on-board isolation resistance monitoring system shall be tested by first determining the isolation resistance Ri of the electric power train with the electrical isolation monitoring system using the procedure outlined in Annex 5A.

If the minimum required isolation resistance is 100 Ω/V, a resistor Ro shall be inserted between the side of the high voltage bus exhibiting the lower value of U1 or U2 and the electrical chassis, with 1/(1/(95xU) - 1/Ri) ≤ Ro < 1/(1/(100xU) - 1/Ri), where U is the working voltage of the electric power train.
condition: if the minimum isolation resistance value required in accordance with paragraphs 5.1.3.1. or 5.1.3.2. is 100 Ω/V

text: If the minimum required isolation resistance is 500 Ω/V, a resistor Ro shall be inserted between the side of the high voltage bus exhibiting the lower value of U1 or U2 and the electrical chassis, with 1/(1/(475xU) - 1/Ri) ≤ Ro < 1/(1/(500xU) - 1/Ri), where U is the working voltage of the electric power train.
condition: if the minimum isolation resistance value required in accordance with paragraphs 5.1.3.1. or 5.1.3.2. is 500 Ω/V

text: The electrical design or components of the vehicle shall comply with the requirements of paragraphs 5.1.1. (protection against direct contact), 5.1.2. (protection against indirect contact) and 5.1.3. (isolation resistance), separately verified by the testing authority.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses document-based compliance according to paragraph 5.1.4.2.

text: Vehicle manufacturers shall provide information to testing authorities to identify, as a point of reference, the mounting location for each high-voltage component in/on the vehicle.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses document-based compliance according to paragraph 5.1.4.2.

text: The documentation shall contain information on how the manufacturer tested isolation resistance compliance of the electrical design of the vehicle by using fresh water.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses document-based compliance according to paragraph 5.1.4.2.

text: The documentation shall contain information on how, after the test, the high-voltage component or system was inspected for ingress of water and how, depending on its mounting location, each high voltage component/system met the appropriate degree of protection against water.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses document-based compliance according to paragraph 5.1.4.2.

text: The testing authority shall verify and confirm the authenticity of the documented conditions observed during the manufacturer's certification process.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses document-based compliance according to paragraph 5.1.4.2.

text: For the water exposure tests, the surface area of the tested high-voltage component or system shall be calculated with an accuracy of 10 per cent; partly condensed moisture and deposited dew inside the enclosure are not considered as ingress of water.
If possible, the tested high-voltage component or system shall be run energized, and if energized adequate safety precautions shall be taken.

For electrical components externally attached and open underneath (exposed or protected locations), the test shall be conducted by spraying the high-voltage component or system from all practicable directions with a stream of water from a standard test nozzle as shown in Figure 1.
condition: for externally attached electrical components open underneath

text: The standard test nozzle internal diameter shall be 6.3 mm.
condition: for externally attached electrical components open underneath

text: The water delivery rate shall be 11.9 - 13.2 l/min.
condition: for externally attached electrical components open underneath

text: The water pressure at the nozzle shall be approximately 30 kPa (0.3 bar).
condition: for externally attached electrical components open underneath

text: The test duration shall be 1 min per m2 of surface area of the tested high-voltage component or system, with a minimum test duration of 3 min.
condition: for externally attached electrical components open underneath

text: The distance from the nozzle to the tested high-voltage component or system surface shall be approximately 3 m, which may be reduced if necessary to ensure proper wetting when spraying upwards.
condition: for externally attached electrical components open underneath

text: For externally attached electrical components covered from underneath, the cover shall protect the component against direct spray water from underneath and shall not be visible.
condition: for externally attached electrical components covered from underneath

text: The test shall be conducted using the splashing test nozzle shown in Figure 2, with the moving shield removed and the machine sprayed from all practicable directions.
condition: for externally attached electrical components covered from underneath

text: The water pressure shall be adjusted to give a delivery rate of (10 ± 0.5) l/min (pressure approximately 80 kPa to 100 kPa (0.8 bar to 1.0 bar)).
condition: for externally attached electrical components covered from underneath

text: The test duration shall be 1 min/m2 of calculated surface area of the machine (excluding any mounting surface and cooling fin) with a minimum duration of 5 min.
condition: for externally attached electrical components covered from underneath

text: The splashing test spray nozzle shall be brass with 121 holes of ⌀ 0.5: 1 hole in centre, inner circle of 12 holes at 30° pitch, outer circle of 24 holes at 15° pitch, with an aluminium moving shield.
condition: for externally attached electrical components covered from underneath

text: After water exposure, the entire high voltage system or each component shall comply with the isolation resistance requirement in paragraph 5.1.3.
For the isolation resistance check, the electric chassis shall be simulated by an electric conductor, e.g. a metal plate, with the components attached with their standard mounting devices.
For the isolation resistance check, cables, where provided, shall be connected to the component.

Parts of the high-voltage component or system designed not to be wet during operation shall not be wet, and no accumulation of water which could have reached them is tolerated inside the high-voltage component or system.

In the washing test, all vehicle border lines (seals of two parts such as flaps, glass seals, outline of opening parts, outline of front grille and seals of lamps) shall be exposed and followed in all directions with the water stream using a hose nozzle and conditions in accordance with IPX5 as specified in Annex 7A.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses the vehicle-based test of paragraph 5.1.4.3.

text: The vehicle shall be driven in a wade pool with 10 cm water depth over a distance of 500 m at a speed of 20 km/h, in a time of approximately 1.5 min.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses the vehicle-based test of paragraph 5.1.4.3.

text: If the wade pool is less than 500 m in length, the vehicle shall be driven through it several times, and the total time including periods outside the wade pool shall be less than 10 min.
condition: if the wade pool is less than 500 m in length

text: The hydrogen emission test shall consist of vehicle/REESS preparation, discharge of the REESS, determination of hydrogen emissions during a normal charge, and determination of hydrogen emissions during a charge carried out with the charger failure.
For the vehicle based hydrogen emission test, the vehicle shall be in good mechanical condition and have been driven at least 300 km during seven days before the test.
condition: vehicle based test

text: The vehicle shall be equipped with the REESS subject to the hydrogen emission test over the 300 km / seven days pre-test period.
condition: vehicle based test

text: If the REESS is used at a temperature above ambient, the operator shall follow the manufacturer's procedure to keep the REESS temperature in its normal functioning range.
condition: vehicle based test; if the REESS is used at a temperature above the ambient temperature

text: The manufacturer's representative shall be able to certify that the temperature conditioning system of the REESS is neither damaged nor presenting a capacity defect.
condition: vehicle based test; if the REESS is used at a temperature above the ambient temperature
