text: For the component based hydrogen emission test, the REESS shall be in good mechanical condition and have been subject to a minimum of 5 standard cycles (as specified in Annex 9, Appendix 1).
condition: component based test

text: If the REESS is used at a temperature above ambient, the operator shall follow the manufacturer's procedure to keep the REESS temperature in its normal functioning range.
condition: component based test; if the REESS is used at a temperature above the ambient temperature

text: The manufacturer's representative shall be able to certify that the temperature conditioning system of the REESS is neither damaged nor presenting a capacity defect.
condition: component based test; if the REESS is used at a temperature above the ambient temperature

text: The chassis dynamometer used for the hydrogen emission test shall meet the requirements of the 06 series of amendments to Regulation No. 83.
The hydrogen emission measurement enclosure shall be a gas-tight measuring chamber able to contain the vehicle/REESS under test, with the vehicle/REESS accessible from all sides.
The enclosure when sealed shall be gas-tight in accordance with Annex 8, Appendix 1.
The inner surface of the enclosure shall be impermeable and non-reactive to hydrogen.

The enclosure temperature conditioning system shall be capable of controlling the internal enclosure air temperature to follow the prescribed temperature throughout the test, with an average tolerance of ±2 K over the duration of the test.
Any design for volume accommodation shall maintain the integrity of the enclosure as specified in Annex 8, Appendix 1.
condition: if a variable-volume or other volume accommodation equipment is used

text: Any method of volume accommodation shall limit the differential between the enclosure internal pressure and the barometric pressure to a maximum value of ±5 hPa.
condition: if a variable-volume or other volume accommodation equipment is used

text: The enclosure shall be capable of latching to a fixed volume.
A variable volume enclosure shall be capable of accommodating a change from its nominal volume, taking into account hydrogen emissions during testing.
condition: for a variable volume enclosure

text: The chamber atmosphere shall be monitored using a hydrogen analyser (electrochemical detector type) or a chromatograph with thermal conductivity detection.
Sample gas shall be drawn from the mid-point of one side-wall or roof of the chamber and any bypass flow shall be returned to the enclosure, preferably immediately downstream of the mixing fan.
The hydrogen analyser shall have a response time to 90 per cent of final reading of less than 10 seconds.
The hydrogen analyser stability shall be better than 2 per cent of full scale at zero and at 80 per cent ± 20 per cent of full scale, over a 15-minute period for all operational ranges.

The repeatability of the hydrogen analyser expressed as one standard deviation shall be better than 1 per cent of full scale, at zero and at 80 per cent ± 20 per cent of full scale on all ranges used.
The operational ranges of the hydrogen analyser shall be chosen to give best resolution over the measurement, calibration and leak checking procedures.
The hydrogen analyser shall be fitted with a device to record electrical signal output at a frequency of at least once per minute.
The hydrogen analyser recording system shall have operating characteristics at least equivalent to the signal being recorded and shall provide a permanent record of results.
The recording shall show a clear indication of the beginning and end of the normal charge test and charging failure operation.

The chamber temperature shall be recorded at two points by temperature sensors connected to show a mean value, with measuring points extended approximately 0.1 m into the enclosure from the vertical centre line of each side-wall at a height of 0.9 ± 0.2 m.
The temperatures in the proximity of the cells shall be recorded by means of sensors.
Temperatures shall, throughout the hydrogen emission measurements, be recorded at a frequency of at least once per minute.
The accuracy of the temperature recording system shall be within ±1.0 K and the temperature shall be capable of being resolved to ±0.1 K.
The temperature recording or data processing system shall be capable of resolving time to ±15 seconds.

The difference Δp between barometric pressure within the test area and the enclosure internal pressure shall, throughout the hydrogen emission measurements, be recorded at a frequency of at least once per minute.
The accuracy of the pressure recording system shall be within ±2 hPa and the pressure shall be capable of being resolved to ±0.2 hPa.
The pressure recording or data processing system shall be capable of resolving time to ±15 seconds.
The charger voltage and current intensity (battery) shall, throughout the hydrogen emission measurements, be recorded at a frequency of at least once per minute.
The accuracy of the voltage recording system shall be within ±1 V and the voltage shall be capable of being resolved to ±0.1 V.
The accuracy of the current intensity recording system shall be within ±0.5 A and the current intensity shall be capable of being resolved to ±0.05 A.
The voltage and current recording or data processing system shall be capable of resolving time to ±15 seconds.
The chamber shall be equipped with one or more fans or blowers with a possible flow of 0.1 to 0.5 m3/second to thoroughly mix the atmosphere in the enclosure.
It shall be possible to reach a homogeneous temperature and hydrogen concentration in the chamber during measurements.
The vehicle in the enclosure shall not be subjected to a direct stream of air from the fans or blowers.
Purified synthetic air (purity < 1 ppm C1 equivalent; < 1 ppm CO; < 400 ppm CO2; < 0.1 ppm NO; oxygen content between 18 and 21 per cent by volume) shall be available for calibration and operation.
Hydrogen (H2) of 99.5 per cent minimum purity shall be available for calibration and operation.
Calibration and span gases shall contain mixtures of hydrogen (H2) and purified synthetic air.
The real concentrations of a calibration gas shall be within ±2 per cent of the nominal values.
The accuracy of diluted gases obtained when using a gas divider shall be within ±2 per cent of the nominal value.
condition: if a gas divider is used

text: The hydrogen emission test shall consist of five steps: vehicle/REESS preparation; discharge of the REESS; determination of hydrogen emissions during a normal charge; discharge of the traction battery; determination of hydrogen emissions during a charge carried out with the charger failure.
If the vehicle/REESS has to be moved between two steps of the hydrogen emission test, it shall be pushed to the following test area.
condition: if the vehicle/REESS has to be moved between two steps

text: For the vehicle based hydrogen emission test, the ageing of the REESS shall be checked, proving that the vehicle has performed at least 300 km during seven days before the test.
condition: vehicle based test

text: During the 300 km / seven days ageing period, the vehicle shall be equipped with the traction battery submitted to the hydrogen emission test; if this cannot be demonstrated, the discharge and initial charge procedure of paragraphs 5.1.1.1 to 5.1.1.3 shall be applied.
condition: vehicle based test

text: The preparation procedure shall start with the discharge of the REESS while driving on the test track or on a chassis dynamometer at a steady speed of 70 ± 5 per cent of the maximum speed of the vehicle during 30 minutes.
condition: vehicle based test where ageing cannot be demonstrated

text: Discharging of the REESS during preparation shall be stopped when the vehicle is not able to run at 65 per cent of the maximum thirty minutes speed, or when an indication to stop the vehicle is given to the driver by the standard on-board instrumentation, or after having covered the distance of 100 km.
condition: vehicle based test where ageing cannot be demonstrated

text: The initial charge of the REESS shall be carried out with the charger, excluding all types of external chargers, in an ambient temperature between 293 K and 303 K.
condition: vehicle based test where ageing cannot be demonstrated

text: The end of the initial REESS charge shall correspond to an automatic stop given by the charger, and the procedure includes all types of special charges that could be automatically or manually initiated (e.g. equalisation or servicing charges).
condition: vehicle based test where ageing cannot be demonstrated

text: The discharge and initial charge procedure of paragraphs 5.1.1.1 and 5.1.1.2 shall be repeated two times.
condition: vehicle based test where ageing cannot be demonstrated

text: The REESS shall be discharged while driving on the test track or on a chassis dynamometer at a steady speed of 70 ± 5 per cent of the maximum thirty minutes speed of the vehicle.
condition: vehicle based test

text: The REESS discharge shall be stopped when an indication to stop the vehicle is given to the driver by the standard on-board instrumentation, or when the maximum speed of the vehicle is lower than 20 km/h.
condition: vehicle based test

text: Within fifteen minutes of completing the battery discharge operation, the vehicle shall be parked in the soak area for a minimum of 12 hours and a maximum of 36 hours between the end of the traction battery discharge and the start of the hydrogen emission test during a normal charge.
condition: vehicle based test

text: During the soak period, the vehicle shall be soaked at 293 K ± 2 K.
condition: vehicle based test

text: Before the completion of the soak period for the normal charge test, the measuring chamber shall be purged for several minutes until a stable hydrogen background is obtained, and the enclosure mixing fan(s) shall be turned on at this time.
condition: vehicle based test, normal charge

text: The hydrogen analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately prior to the normal charge test.
condition: vehicle based test, normal charge

text: At the end of the soak, the test vehicle, with the engine shut off and the windows and luggage compartment opened, shall be moved into the measuring chamber.
condition: vehicle based test, normal charge

text: The vehicle shall be connected to the mains and the REESS charged according to the normal charge procedure of paragraph 5.1.4.7.
condition: vehicle based test, normal charge

text: The enclosure doors shall be closed and sealed gas-tight within two minutes from electrical interlock of the normal charge step.
condition: vehicle based test, normal charge

text: The normal charge hydrogen emission test period shall begin when the chamber is sealed, and the hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure shall be measured to give the initial readings CH2i, Ti and Pi.
condition: vehicle based test, normal charge

text: The ambient enclosure temperature T shall not be less than 291 K and no more than 295 K during the normal charge period.
condition: vehicle based test, normal charge

text: The normal charge shall be carried out with the charger and consist of charging at constant power during t1 followed by over-charging at constant current during t2, the over-charging intensity being specified by the manufacturer and corresponding to that used during equalisation charging.
condition: vehicle based test, normal charge

text: The end of the normal REESS charge shall correspond to an automatic stop given by the charger at a charging time of t1 + t2, limited to t1 + 5 h even if the standard instrumentation indicates that the battery is not yet fully charged.
condition: vehicle based test, normal charge

text: The hydrogen analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately before the end of the normal charge test.
condition: vehicle based test, normal charge

text: The emission sampling period shall end t1 + t2 or t1 + 5 hours after the beginning of the initial sampling; the elapsed times shall be recorded and the hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure measured to give the final readings CH2f, Tf and Pf for the normal charge test.
condition: vehicle based test, normal charge

text: Within seven days maximum after completing the normal charge test, the charger failure test procedure shall start with the discharge of the REESS of the vehicle according to Annex 8 paragraph 5.1.2.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: The soak procedure of Annex 8 paragraph 5.1.3 shall be repeated for the charger failure test.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: Before the completion of the soak period for the charger failure test, the measuring chamber shall be purged for several minutes until a stable hydrogen background is obtained, and the enclosure mixing fan(s) shall be turned on at this time.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: The hydrogen analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately prior to the charger failure test.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: At the end of the soak, the test vehicle, with the engine shut off and the windows and luggage compartment opened, shall be moved into the measuring chamber for the charger failure test.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: The vehicle shall be connected to the mains and the REESS charged according to the failure charge procedure of paragraph 5.1.5.9.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: The enclosure doors shall be closed and sealed gas-tight within two minutes from electrical interlock of the failure charge step.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: The failure charge hydrogen emission test period shall begin when the chamber is sealed, and the hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure shall be measured to give the initial readings CH2i, Ti and Pi.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: The ambient enclosure temperature T shall not be less than 291 K and no more than 295 K during the charging failure period.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: The charging failure shall be carried out with the suitable charger and consist of charging at constant power during t'1 followed by charging at maximum current as recommended by the manufacturer during 30 minutes.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: During the 30-minute maximum current phase, the charger shall supply maximum current as recommended by the manufacturer.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: The hydrogen analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately before the end of the charger failure test.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: The charger failure test period shall end t'1 + 30 minutes after the beginning of the initial sampling; the elapsed times shall be recorded and the hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure measured to give the final readings CH2f, Tf and Pf.
condition: vehicle based test, charger failure

text: For the component based hydrogen emission test, the ageing of the REESS shall be checked to confirm that the REESS has performed at least 5 standard cycles.
condition: component based test

text: The REESS shall be discharged at 70 ± 5 per cent of the nominal power of the system, the discharge being stopped when the minimum SOC specified by the manufacturer is reached.
condition: component based test

text: Within 15 minutes of the end of the REESS discharge and before the start of the hydrogen emission test, the REESS shall be soaked at 293 ± 2 K for a minimum of 12 hours and a maximum of 36 hours.
condition: component based test

text: Before the completion of the REESS soak period for the normal charge test, the measuring chamber shall be purged for several minutes until a stable hydrogen background is obtained, and the enclosure mixing fan(s) shall be turned on at this time.
condition: component based test, normal charge

text: The hydrogen analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately prior to the component based normal charge test.
condition: component based test, normal charge

text: At the end of the soak period, the REESS shall be moved into the measuring chamber.
condition: component based test, normal charge

text: The REESS shall be charged in accordance with the normal charge procedure of paragraph 5.2.4.7.
condition: component based test, normal charge

text: The chamber shall be closed and sealed gas-tight within two minutes of the electrical interlock of the normal charge step.
condition: component based test, normal charge

text: The normal charge hydrogen emission test period shall begin when the chamber is sealed, and the hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure shall be measured to give the initial readings CH2i, Ti and Pi.
condition: component based test, normal charge

text: The ambient enclosure temperature T shall not be less than 291 K and no more than 295 K during the normal charge period.
condition: component based test, normal charge

text: The normal charge shall be carried out with a suitable charger and consist of charging at constant power during t1 followed by over-charging at constant current during t2, the over-charging intensity being specified by the manufacturer and corresponding to that used during equalisation charging.
condition: component based test, normal charge

text: The end of the normal REESS charge shall correspond to an automatic stop given by the charger at a charging time of t1 + t2, limited to t1 + 5 h even if a suitable instrumentation indicates that the REESS is not yet fully charged.
condition: component based test, normal charge

text: The hydrogen analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately before the end of the component based normal charge test.
condition: component based test, normal charge

text: The emission sampling period shall end t1 + t2 or t1 + 5 h after the beginning of the initial sampling; the elapsed times shall be recorded and the hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure measured to give the final readings CH2f, Tf and Pf for the normal charge test.
condition: component based test, normal charge

text: The charger failure test procedure shall start within a maximum of seven days after completing the normal charge test, with the discharge of the REESS in accordance with paragraph 5.2.2.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: The soak procedure of paragraph 5.2.3 shall be repeated for the component based charger failure test.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: Before the completion of the soak period for the charger failure test, the measuring chamber shall be purged for several minutes until a stable hydrogen background is obtained, and the enclosure mixing fan(s) shall be turned on at this time.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: The hydrogen analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately prior to the component based charger failure test.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: At the end of the soak, the REESS shall be moved into the measuring chamber for the charger failure test.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: The REESS shall be charged according to the failure charge procedure of paragraph 5.2.5.9.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: The chamber shall be closed and sealed gas-tight within two minutes from electrical interlock of the failure charge step.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: The failure charge hydrogen emission test period shall begin when the chamber is sealed, and the hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure shall be measured to give the initial readings CH2i, Ti and Pi.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: The ambient enclosure temperature T shall not be less than 291 K and no more than 295 K during the charging failure period.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: The charging failure shall be carried out with a suitable charger and consist of charging at constant power during t'1 followed by charging at maximum current as recommended by the manufacturer during 30 minutes.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: During the 30-minute maximum current phase, the charger shall supply maximum current as recommended by the manufacturer.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: The hydrogen analyser shall be zeroed and spanned immediately before the end of the component based charger failure test.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: The charger failure test period shall end t'1 + 30 minutes after the beginning of the initial sampling; the elapsed times shall be recorded and the hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure measured to give the final readings CH2f, Tf and Pf.
condition: component based test, charger failure

text: Hydrogen emissions from the normal charge and charging failure phases shall be calculated from the initial and final hydrogen concentrations, temperatures and pressures in the enclosure together with the net enclosure volume (corrected for the vehicle volume with windows and luggage compartment open, or by subtracting 1.42 m³ if the vehicle volume is not determined), using k = 2.42.
The hydrogen mass emission results for the REESS shall be expressed as MN (normal charge test, in grams) and MD (charging failure test, in grams).

All hydrogen emission test equipment shall be calibrated before its initial use and then as often as necessary and in any case in the month before type approval testing, using the calibration methods described in Annex 8 Appendix 1.

Before its initial use, the internal volume of the hydrogen emission measurement chamber shall be determined from careful measurement of its internal dimensions, taking into account any irregularities such as bracing struts.
The enclosure shall be latched to a fixed volume when held at an ambient temperature of 293 K, and this nominal volume shall be repeatable within ±0.5 per cent of the reported value.

The net internal volume of the chamber is determined by subtracting 1.42 m3 from the internal volume of the chamber; alternatively the volume of the test vehicle with the luggage compartment and windows open, or of the REESS, may be used instead of the 1.42 m3.
The chamber shall be checked as in Annex 8, paragraph 2.3; if the hydrogen mass does not agree with the injected mass to within ±2 per cent, corrective action is required.

The chamber background emission check shall be carried out at the enclosure's introduction to service, after any operations in the enclosure which may affect background emissions and at a frequency of at least once per year.

During the background emission determination, the ambient temperature shall be maintained at 293 K ± 2 K throughout the four-hour period; a variable-volume enclosure may be operated in either latched or unlatched volume configuration.
The enclosure may be sealed and the mixing fan operated for a period of up to 12 hours before the four-hour background-sampling period begins.
For the background emission check, the hydrogen analyser (if required) shall be calibrated, then zeroed and spanned.
For the background emission check, the enclosure shall be purged until a stable hydrogen reading is obtained, and the mixing fan turned on if not already on.

The chamber is then sealed and the background hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure are measured as the initial readings CH2i, Ti and Pi for the enclosure background calculation.
The enclosure is allowed to stand undisturbed with the mixing fan on for a period of four hours.

At the end of the four hours the same analyser is used to measure the hydrogen concentration in the chamber, and temperature and barometric pressure are measured, as the final readings CH2f, Tf and Pf.
The change in mass of hydrogen in the enclosure shall be calculated over the time of the background test in accordance with Annex 8, paragraph 2.4 and shall not exceed 0.5 g.

The enclosure leak rate shall be determined at the enclosure's introduction to service, after any operations in the enclosure which may affect the integrity of the enclosure, and at least monthly thereafter.

The enclosure leak rate may be determined quarterly as long as no corrective action is required, provided six consecutive monthly retention checks have been successfully completed without corrective action.
condition: if six consecutive monthly retention checks are successfully completed without corrective action

text: For the calibration and hydrogen retention test, the enclosure shall be purged until a stable hydrogen concentration is reached, the mixing fan turned on, and the hydrogen analyser zeroed, calibrated if required, and spanned.
For the calibration and hydrogen retention test, the enclosure shall be latched to the nominal volume position.
The ambient temperature control system is turned on (if not already on) and adjusted for an initial temperature of 293 K.

When the enclosure temperature stabilizes at 293 K ± 2 K, the enclosure is sealed and the background concentration, temperature and barometric pressure measured as initial readings CH2i, Ti and Pi for the enclosure calibration.
For the calibration and hydrogen retention test, the enclosure shall be unlatched from the nominal volume.
A quantity of approximately 100 g of hydrogen is injected into the enclosure, and this mass of hydrogen shall be measured to an accuracy of ±2 per cent of the measured value.

The contents of the chamber shall be allowed to mix for five minutes, then the hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure are measured as final readings for calibration and initial readings for the retention check.

The mass of hydrogen in the enclosure calculated from the readings of paragraphs 2.3.4 and 2.3.7 using the formula in paragraph 2.4 shall be within ±2 per cent of the mass of hydrogen measured in paragraph 2.3.6.

The contents of the chamber shall be allowed to mix for a minimum of 10 hours, after which the final hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure are measured and recorded for the hydrogen retention check.
The hydrogen mass calculated from the readings of paragraphs 2.3.7 and 2.3.9 may not differ by more than 5 per cent from the hydrogen mass given by paragraph 2.3.8.

The net hydrogen mass change within the enclosure shall be calculated from initial and final readings of hydrogen concentration, temperature and barometric pressure using the prescribed formula with k = 2.42 and V the enclosure volume as measured in paragraph 2.1.1.
Each of the normally used operating ranges of the hydrogen analyser shall be calibrated using hydrogen in air and purified synthetic air according to the prescribed procedure.

The hydrogen analyser calibration curve shall be established by at least five calibration points spaced as evenly as possible over the operating range, the highest calibration gas nominal concentration being at least 80 per cent of the full scale.
The calibration curve shall be calculated by the method of least squares.
The number of calibration points shall be at least the number of the polynomial degree plus two.
condition: if the resulting polynomial degree is greater than three

text: The calibration curve shall not differ by more than two per cent from the nominal value of each calibration gas.
For each analyser range calibrated, a table of analyser readings against true concentrations shall be drawn using the polynomial coefficients by steps no greater than 1 per cent of full scale.

The analyser calibration table shall also contain relevant data such as date of calibration, span and zero potentiometer readings (where applicable), nominal scale, reference data of each calibration gas, real and indicated value of each calibration gas with percentage differences, and calibration pressure of analyser.
Alternative analyser calibration methods (e.g. computer, electronically controlled range switch) may be used only if it is proven to the technical service that they give equivalent accuracy.
condition: if alternative calibration methods are used

text: A vehicle family relative to hydrogen emissions shall be defined by basic design parameters common to vehicles within the family, taking interaction of parameters into consideration so that only vehicles with similar hydrogen emission characteristics are included.
condition: if approval is extended to a family of vehicle types

text: Vehicle types belong to the same hydrogen emission family only if the REESS parameters are identical: trade name or mark, types of electrochemical couples, number of cells, number of REESS subsystems, nominal voltage, REESS energy, gas combination rate, type(s) of ventilation for REESS subsystem(s), and type of cooling system (if any).
condition: if approval is extended to a family of vehicle types

text: Vehicle types belong to the same hydrogen emission family only if the on-board charger parameters are identical: make and type of charger parts, output nominal power, maximum voltage of charge, maximum intensity of charge, make and type of control unit (if any), diagram of operating, controls and safety, and characteristics of charge periods.
condition: if approval is extended to a family of vehicle types

text: A standard cycle shall start with a standard discharge followed by a standard charge and shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 20 ± 10 °C.

The standard discharge procedure including termination criteria shall be defined by the manufacturer; if not specified, it shall be a discharge with 1C current for a complete REESS and REESS subsystems, to a discharge limit (end voltage) specified by the manufacturer.
For a complete vehicle, the standard discharge procedure using a dynamometer shall be defined by the manufacturer, with termination according to vehicle controls.
condition: for a complete vehicle

text: The rest period after standard discharge shall be minimum 15 min.

The standard charge procedure shall be defined by the manufacturer; if not specified, it shall be a charge with C/3 current continued until normally terminated, with termination according to paragraph 2 of Annex 9, Appendix 2 for REESS or REESS subsystem.

For a complete vehicle that can be charged by an external source, the standard charge procedure using an external electric power supply shall be defined by the manufacturer, with termination according to vehicle controls.
condition: for a complete vehicle chargeable by an external source

text: For a complete vehicle that can be charged by on-board energy sources, a standard charge procedure using a dynamometer shall be defined by the manufacturer, with termination according to vehicle controls.
condition: for a complete vehicle chargeable by on-board energy sources

text: The adjustment of SOC shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 20 ± 10 °C for vehicle-based tests and 22 ± 5 °C for component-based tests.
Where different charging procedures are possible, the REESS shall be charged using the procedure which yields the highest SOC.
condition: where different charging procedures are possible

text: For a vehicle with a REESS designed to be externally charged, the REESS shall be charged to the highest SOC in accordance with the manufacturer's procedure for normal operation until the charging process is normally terminated.
condition: REESS designed to be externally charged, vehicle-based test

text: For a vehicle with a REESS designed to be charged only by an energy source on the vehicle, the REESS shall be charged to the highest SOC achievable with normal operation of the vehicle, and the manufacturer shall advise on the vehicle operation mode to achieve this SOC.
condition: REESS designed to be charged only by an on-board energy source

text: Where the REESS or REESS subsystem is used as the Tested-Device, it shall be charged to the highest SOC in accordance with the manufacturer's procedure for normal use operation until the charging process is normally terminated; manufacturing, service or maintenance procedures may be used only if they achieve an equivalent SOC.
condition: REESS or REESS subsystem used as Tested-Device

text: Where the Tested-Device does not control SOC by itself, the SOC shall be charged to not less than 95 per cent of the maximum normal operating SOC defined by the manufacturer for the specific configuration of the Tested-Device.
condition: Tested-Device does not control SOC by itself

text: When the vehicle or REESS subsystem is tested, the SOC shall be no less than 95 per cent of the SOC according to paragraphs 1 and 2 for REESS designed to be externally charged.
condition: REESS designed to be externally charged

text: When the vehicle or REESS subsystem is tested, the SOC shall be no less than 90 per cent of the SOC according to paragraphs 1 and 2 for REESS designed to be charged only by an energy source on the vehicle.
condition: REESS designed to be charged only by an on-board energy source

text: The SOC shall be confirmed by a method provided by the manufacturer.
The vibration test shall be conducted either with the complete REESS or with REESS subsystem(s).

If the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s) in the vibration test, the manufacturer shall demonstrate that the test result can reasonably represent the performance of the complete REESS with respect to its safety performance under the same conditions.
condition: if tested with REESS subsystem(s)

text: The electronic management unit may be omitted from the vibration Tested-Device on request of the manufacturer only if it is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells.
condition: if the electronic management unit is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells

text: The Tested-Device shall be firmly secured to the platform of the vibration machine so that vibrations are directly transmitted to it, and should be mounted with its original mounting points, if existing, as mounted in the vehicle.
The vibration test shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 22 ± 5 °C.
At the beginning of the vibration test, the SOC shall be adjusted to a value in accordance with Annex 9, Appendix 2.
At the beginning of the vibration test, all protection devices which affect the function(s) of the tested-device that are relevant to the outcome of the test shall be operational.

The Tested-Device shall be subjected to a sinusoidal vibration with a logarithmic sweep between 7 Hz and 50 Hz and back to 7 Hz traversed in 15 minutes, repeated 12 times for a total of 3 hours in the vertical direction of the mounting orientation of the REESS as specified by the manufacturer.
In the vibration test, the acceleration shall be 10 m/s2 for frequencies 7 - 18 Hz.
In the vibration test, the acceleration shall be gradually reduced from 10 to 2 m/s2 for frequencies 18 - 30 Hz.
In the vibration test, the acceleration shall be 2 m/s2 for frequencies 30 - 50 Hz.
At the request of the manufacturer, a higher acceleration level and a higher maximum frequency may be used in the vibration test.
condition: at the request of the manufacturer

text: A vibration test profile determined by the vehicle manufacturer may substitute Table 1 only if verified for the vehicle application and agreed with the Technical Service, and the approval of a REESS so tested shall be limited to installation for a specific vehicle type.
condition: if a vehicle-specific vibration profile is used at the manufacturer's request

text: After the vibration, a standard cycle shall be conducted, if not inhibited by the tested-device.
condition: if not inhibited by the tested-device

text: The vibration test shall end with an observation period of 1 h at the ambient temperature conditions of the test environment.
In the thermal shock test the REESS shall undergo a specified number of temperature cycles starting at ambient temperature followed by high and low temperature cycling.
The thermal shock and cycling test shall be conducted either with the complete REESS or with REESS subsystem(s) including the cells and their electrical connections.

If the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s) in the thermal shock and cycling test, the manufacturer shall demonstrate that the test result can reasonably represent the performance of the complete REESS with respect to its safety performance under the same conditions.
condition: if tested with REESS subsystem(s)

text: The electronic management unit may be omitted from the thermal shock Tested-Device on request of the manufacturer only if it is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells.
condition: if the electronic management unit is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells

text: At the start of the thermal shock and cycling test, the SOC shall be adjusted in accordance with Annex 9, Appendix 2.
At the start of the thermal shock and cycling test, all protection devices which would affect the function of the Tested-Device and which are relevant to the outcome of the test shall be operational.

The Tested-Device shall be stored for at least six hours at a test temperature equal to 60 ± 2 °C or higher if requested by the manufacturer, followed by storage for at least six hours at -40 ± 2 °C or lower if requested by the manufacturer.
The maximum time interval between test temperature extremes shall be 30 minutes.
The temperature cycling procedure shall be repeated until a minimum of 5 total cycles are completed, after which the tested-device shall be stored for 24 hours at an ambient temperature of 22 ± 5 °C.
After the storage for 24 hours, a standard cycle as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 shall be conducted, if not inhibited by the tested-device.
condition: if not inhibited by the tested-device

text: The thermal shock and cycling test shall end with an observation period of 1 h at the ambient temperature conditions of the test environment.
The mechanical shock test shall be conducted either with the complete REESS or with REESS subsystem(s).

If the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s) in the mechanical shock test, the manufacturer shall demonstrate that the test result can reasonably represent the performance of the complete REESS with respect to its safety performance under the same conditions.
condition: if tested with REESS subsystem(s)

text: The electronic management unit may be omitted from the mechanical shock Tested-Device on request of the manufacturer only if it is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells.
condition: if the electronic management unit is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells

text: In the mechanical shock test, the tested-device shall be connected to the test fixture only by the intended mountings provided for attaching the REESS or REESS subsystem to the vehicle.
The mechanical shock test shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 20 ± 10 °C.
At the beginning of the mechanical shock test, the SOC of the Tested-Device shall be adjusted in accordance with Annex 9, Appendix 2.
At the beginning of the mechanical shock test, all protection devices which affect the function of the Tested-Device and which are relevant to the outcome of the test shall be operational.

In the mechanical shock test the Tested-Device shall be decelerated or accelerated in compliance with the acceleration corridors specified in Tables 1 to 3, the test pulse being within the minimum and maximum values specified in those tables.
The manufacturer shall decide whether the mechanical shock tests are conducted in the positive or negative direction or both.
A separate Tested-Device may be used for each of the specified mechanical shock test pulses.
A higher shock level and/or longer duration than the maximum value in Tables 1 to 3 may be applied to the Tested-Device only if recommended by the manufacturer.
condition: if recommended by the manufacturer

text: The mechanical shock test shall end with an observation period of 1 hour at the ambient temperature conditions of the test environment.

For REESS of M1, N1, O1 and O2 vehicles, the minimum mechanical shock pulse corridor shall be: A 20 ms 0 g; B 50 ms 20 g longitudinal / 8 g transverse; C 65 ms 20 g longitudinal / 8 g transverse; D 100 ms 0 g.

For REESS of M1, N1, O1 and O2 vehicles, the maximum mechanical shock pulse corridor shall be: E 0 ms 10 g longitudinal / 4.5 g transverse; F 50 ms 28 g longitudinal / 15 g transverse; G 80 ms 28 g longitudinal / 15 g transverse; H 120 ms 0 g.

For vehicles of category O1 and O2, at the request of the manufacturer, the pulses of Table 2 of Annex 9C paragraph 3.2 may be used only if the maximum design speed of these vehicles is limited to 100 km/h.
condition: at the request of the manufacturer and if the maximum design speed is limited to 100 km/h

text: For REESS of M2 and N2 vehicles, the minimum mechanical shock pulse corridor shall be: A 20 ms 0 g; B 50 ms 10 g longitudinal / 5 g transverse; C 65 ms 10 g longitudinal / 5 g transverse; D 100 ms 0 g.

For REESS of M2 and N2 vehicles, the maximum mechanical shock pulse corridor shall be: E 0 ms 5 g longitudinal / 2.5 g transverse; F 50 ms 17 g longitudinal / 10 g transverse; G 80 ms 17 g longitudinal / 10 g transverse; H 120 ms 0 g.

For REESS of M3, N3, O3 and O4 vehicles, the minimum mechanical shock pulse corridor shall be: A 20 ms 0 g; B 50 ms 6,6 g longitudinal / 5 g transverse; C 65 ms 6,6 g longitudinal / 5 g transverse; D 100 ms 0 g.

For REESS of M3, N3, O3 and O4 vehicles, the maximum mechanical shock pulse corridor shall be: E 0 ms 4 g longitudinal / 2.5 g transverse; F 50 ms 12 g longitudinal / 10 g transverse; G 80 ms 12 g longitudinal / 10 g transverse; H 120 ms 0 g.
The mechanical shock test shall end with an observation period of 1 hour at the ambient temperature conditions of the test environment.
The mechanical integrity test shall be conducted either with the complete REESS or with REESS subsystem(s).

If the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s) in the mechanical integrity test, the manufacturer shall demonstrate that the test result can reasonably represent the performance of the complete REESS with respect to its safety performance under the same conditions.
condition: if the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s)

text: The electronic management unit for the REESS may be omitted from the tested-device in the mechanical integrity test only if it is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells and the manufacturer so requests.
condition: if the electronic management unit is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells and requested by the manufacturer

text: For the mechanical integrity test, the tested-device shall be connected to the test fixture as recommended by the manufacturer.
The mechanical integrity test shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 20 ± 10 °C.
At the beginning of the mechanical integrity test, the SOC shall be adjusted in accordance with Annex 9, Appendix 2.

At the beginning of the mechanical integrity test, all internal and external protection devices which would affect the function of the Tested-Device and which are relevant to the outcome of the test shall be operational.

Where paragraph 6.4.2.1.2. is applied, vehicle body structure, electrical protection barriers, enclosures, or other mechanical functional devices providing protection against contact may be attached to the Tested-Device if so requested by the manufacturer.
condition: where paragraph 6.4.2.1.2. is applied and requested by the manufacturer

text: Where paragraph 6.4.2.1.2. is applied, the manufacturer shall define the relevant parts used for the mechanical protection of the REESS; the test may be conducted with the REESS mounted to this vehicle structure in a way representative of its mounting in the vehicle.
condition: where paragraph 6.4.2.1.2. is applied

text: The Tested-Device shall be crushed between a resistance and a crush plate with a force of at least 100 kN but not exceeding 105 kN, unless otherwise specified in accordance with paragraph 6.4.2, with an onset time less than 3 minutes and a hold time of at least 100 ms but not exceeding 10 s.
A higher crush force, a longer onset time, a longer hold time, or a combination of these may be applied only at the request of the manufacturer.
condition: at the request of the manufacturer

text: The application of the crush force shall be decided by the manufacturer together with the technical service considering the direction of travel of the REESS relative to its installation in the vehicle, applied horizontally in the direction of travel and horizontally perpendicular to the direction of travel of the REESS.
A separate test-device may be used for each crush test direction.
The crush test shall end with an observation period of 1 h at the ambient temperature conditions of the test environment.

The fire resistance test shall be conducted either with the complete REESS or with REESS subsystem(s); if REESS subsystem(s) are used, the manufacturer shall demonstrate that the test result can reasonably represent the performance of the complete REESS with respect to its safety performance under the same conditions.

In the fire resistance test, the electronic management unit for the REESS may be omitted from the tested-device only if it is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells and the manufacturer so requests.
condition: if the electronic management unit is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells and requested by the manufacturer

text: Where the relevant REESS subsystems are distributed throughout the vehicle, the fire resistance test may be conducted on each relevant REESS subsystem.
condition: where the relevant REESS subsystems are distributed throughout the vehicle

text: The fire resistance test shall be conducted at a temperature of at least 0 °C.
At the beginning of the fire resistance test, the SOC shall be adjusted in accordance with Annex 9, Appendix 2.
At the beginning of the fire resistance test, all protection devices which affect the function of the Tested-Device and are relevant for the outcome of the test shall be operational.
A vehicle based or a component based fire resistance test shall be performed at the discretion of the manufacturer.

In the vehicle based fire resistance test, the tested-device shall be mounted in a testing fixture simulating actual mounting conditions as far as possible, without combustible material other than material that is part of the REESS.
condition: vehicle based test

text: The method whereby the tested-device is fixed in the fixture shall correspond to the relevant specifications for its installation in a vehicle.
condition: vehicle based test

text: In the case of a REESS designed for a specific vehicle use, vehicle parts which affect the course of the fire in any way shall be taken into consideration in the fire resistance test.
condition: REESS designed for a specific vehicle use

text: In the component based fire resistance test, the manufacturer may choose either the gasoline pool fire test or the LPG burner test.
condition: component based test

text: In the component based fire resistance test, the Tested-Device shall be placed on a grating table positioned above the pan, in an orientation according to the manufacturer's design intent.
condition: component based test

text: The grating table shall be constructed of steel rods of diameter 6-10 mm with 4-6 cm in between; the rods may be supported by flat steel parts if needed.
condition: component based test

text: In the gasoline pool fire test, the flame shall be obtained by burning commercial fuel for positive-ignition engines in a pan, in a quantity sufficient for the flame to burn under free-burning conditions for the whole test procedure.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: In the gasoline pool fire test, the fire shall cover the whole area of the pan during the whole fire exposure.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: The pan shall exceed the horizontal projection of the tested-device by at least 20 cm but not more than 50 cm, so that the sides of the tested-device are exposed to the flame.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: The sidewalls of the pan shall not project more than 8 cm above the level of the fuel at the start of the test.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: The fuel pan shall be placed under the tested-device such that the distance between the fuel level and the bottom of the tested-device corresponds to the design height of the tested-device above the road surface at unladen mass for the vehicle based test, or approximately 50 cm for the component based test.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: Either the pan, or the testing fixture, or both, shall be freely movable.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: During phase C of the gasoline pool fire test, the pan shall be covered by a screen placed 3 cm +/- 1 cm above the fuel level measured prior to ignition.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: The screen shall be made of a refractory material as prescribed in Annex 9E - Appendix 1 (firebricks: fire resistance SK 30, Al2O3 content 30 - 33 per cent, open porosity 20 - 22 per cent vol., density 1,900 - 2,000 kg/m3, effective holed area 44.18 per cent).
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: There shall be no gap between the screen bricks and they shall be supported over the fuel pan so that the holes in the bricks are not obstructed.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: The length and width of the screen frame shall be 2 cm to 4 cm smaller than the interior dimensions of the pan so that a gap of 1 cm to 2 cm exists between the frame and the pan wall for ventilation.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: Before the test the screen shall be at least at the ambient temperature; the firebricks may be wetted to guarantee repeatable test conditions.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: If the fire resistance tests are carried out in the open air, sufficient wind protection shall be provided and the wind velocity at pan level shall not exceed 2.5 km/h.
condition: if tests are carried out in the open air

text: The gasoline pool fire test shall comprise three phases B-D if the fuel is at a temperature of at least 20 °C, otherwise four phases A-D.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: In phase A, the fuel in the pan shall be ignited at a distance of at least 3 m from the tested-device and, after 60 seconds pre-heating, the pan shall be placed under the tested-device (or the tested-device and rig moved over the pan if the pan is too large to move safely).
condition: if fuel temperature is below 20 °C

text: In phase B, the tested-device shall be exposed to the flame from the freely burning fuel for 70 seconds.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: In phase C, as soon as phase B has been completed, the screen shall be placed between the burning pan and the tested-device, and the tested-device shall be exposed to this reduced flame for a further 60 seconds.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: In phase D, the burning pan covered with the screen shall be moved back to the phase A position and no extinguishing of the tested-device shall be done.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: After removal of the pan, the tested-device shall be observed until its surface temperature has decreased to ambient temperature or has been decreasing for a minimum of 3 hours.
condition: gasoline pool fire test

text: In the LPG burner fire test, the Tested-Device shall be placed on a test equipment in the position that the manufacturer's design intends.
condition: LPG burner component based test

text: An LPG burner shall be used to produce the flame, with a flame height of about 60 cm or more without the Tested-Device.
condition: LPG burner component based test

text: The flame temperature shall be measured continuously by temperature sensors, and an average temperature shall be calculated at least every second for the whole fire exposure as the arithmetic average of all sensors meeting the location requirements of paragraph 3.4.4.
condition: LPG burner component based test

text: All flame temperature sensors shall be installed at a height of 5 ± 1 cm below the lowest point of the Tested-Device's external surface.
condition: LPG burner component based test

text: At least one temperature sensor shall be located at the centre of the Tested-Device, and at least four temperature sensors shall be located within 10 cm from the edge of the Tested-Device towards its centre with nearly equal distance between the sensors.
condition: LPG burner component based test

text: The bottom of the Tested-Device shall be exposed to the even flame directly and entirely by fuel combustion.
condition: LPG burner component based test

text: The LPG burner flame shall exceed the horizontal projection of the Tested-Device by at least 20 cm.
condition: LPG burner component based test

text: In the LPG burner test, an average temperature of 800 °C shall be reached within 30 seconds and maintained between 800 °C and 1,100 °C, and the Tested-Device shall then be exposed to the flame for 2 minutes.
condition: LPG burner component based test

text: After direct exposure to the LPG flame, the Tested-Device shall be observed until its surface temperature has decreased to ambient temperature or has been decreasing for a minimum of 3 hours.
condition: LPG burner component based test

text: The external short circuit test shall be conducted either with a complete vehicle, with the complete REESS or with the REESS subsystem(s).
If the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s), the Tested-Device shall be able to deliver the nominal voltage of the complete REESS.
condition: if tested with REESS subsystem(s)

text: If the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s), the manufacturer shall demonstrate that the test result can reasonably represent the performance of the complete REESS with respect to its safety performance under the same conditions.
condition: if tested with REESS subsystem(s)

text: In the external short circuit test, the electronic management unit for the REESS may be omitted from the Tested-Device only if it is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells and the manufacturer so requests.
condition: if the electronic management unit is not integrated in the casing enclosing the cells and requested by the manufacturer

text: For a test with a complete vehicle, the manufacturer may provide information to connect a breakout harness to a location just outside the REESS that would permit applying a short circuit to the REESS.
condition: test with a complete vehicle

text: The external short circuit test shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 20 ± 10 °C or at higher temperature if requested by the manufacturer.
At the beginning of the external short circuit test, the SOC shall be adjusted in accordance with Annex 9, Appendix 2.

At the beginning of the external short circuit test, all protection devices which would affect the function of the Tested-Device and which are relevant to the outcome of the test shall be operational.
For testing with a complete vehicle, a breakout harness is connected to the manufacturer specified location and vehicle protection systems relevant to the outcome of the test shall be operational.
condition: testing with a complete vehicle

text: At the start of the external short circuit test all relevant main contactors for charging and discharging shall be closed to represent the active driving possible mode as well as the mode to enable external charging; if this cannot be completed in a single test, two or more tests shall be conducted.

For testing with a complete REESS or REESS subsystem(s), the positive and negative terminals of the Tested-Device shall be connected to each other to produce a short circuit, through a connection with a resistance not exceeding 5 mΩ.
condition: testing with a complete REESS or REESS subsystem(s)

text: For testing with a complete vehicle, the short circuit is applied through the breakout harness and the connection used for creating the short circuit (including the cabling) shall have a resistance not exceeding 5 mΩ.
condition: testing with a complete vehicle

text: The short circuit condition shall be continued until the protection function of the REESS terminates the short circuit current, or for at least 1 hour after the temperature measured on the casing of the Tested-Device has stabilised such that the temperature gradient varies by less than 4 °C through 2 hours.
Directly after the termination of the short circuit, a standard cycle as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 shall be conducted, if not inhibited by the Tested-Device.
condition: if not inhibited by the Tested-Device

text: The external short circuit test shall end with an observation period of 1 h at the ambient temperature conditions of the test environment.
The overcharge protection test shall be conducted, under standard operating conditions, either with a complete vehicle or with the complete REESS.
Ancillary systems that do not influence the overcharge test results may be omitted from the Tested-Device.
The overcharge protection test may be performed with a modified Tested-Device provided these modifications shall not influence the test results.
condition: if a modified Tested-Device is used

text: The overcharge protection test shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 20 ± 10 °C or at higher temperature if requested by the manufacturer.

For the overcharge protection test, the SOC of the REESS shall be adjusted around the middle of normal operating range by normal operation recommended by the manufacturer; accurate adjustment is not required as long as normal operation of the REESS is enabled.
For vehicle-based overcharge test of vehicles with on-board energy conversion systems, the fuel shall be filled to allow the operation of such energy conversion systems.
condition: vehicle-based test of vehicles with on-board energy conversion systems

text: At the beginning of the overcharge test, all protection devices which would affect the function of the Tested-Device and which are relevant to the outcome of the test shall be operational.
At the beginning of the overcharge test, all relevant main contactors for charging shall be closed.

The procedure for charging the REESS for the vehicle-based overcharge test shall be in accordance with paragraphs 3.2.1. and 3.2.2., selected as appropriate for the relevant mode of vehicle operation and the functionality of the protection system, or alternatively in accordance with paragraph 3.2.3.
condition: vehicle-based test

text: For the component-based overcharge test, the charging procedure shall be in accordance with paragraph 3.2.4.
condition: component-based test

text: For vehicles that can be charged by on-board energy sources, the vehicle shall be driven on a chassis dynamometer in active driving possible mode with an operation (e.g. simulation of continuous down-hill driving) delivering as high charging current as reasonably achievable, determined if necessary through consultation with the manufacturer.
condition: vehicle-based test, charge by vehicle operation, vehicles chargeable by on-board energy sources

text: In the charge by vehicle operation procedure, the vehicle operation on the chassis dynamometer shall be terminated when the vehicle's overcharge protection controls terminate the REESS charge current or the REESS temperature is stabilized such that it varies by a gradient of less than 2 °C through 1 hour.
condition: charge by vehicle operation

text: Where the vehicle's overcharge protection control fails to operate or there is no such control, charging by vehicle operation shall be continued until the REESS temperature reaches 10 °C above its maximum operating temperature specified by the manufacturer.
condition: charge by vehicle operation; overcharge protection control fails or absent

text: Immediately after termination of charging by vehicle operation, one standard cycle as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 shall be conducted with vehicle operation on a chassis dynamometer, if not prohibited by the vehicle.
condition: charge by vehicle operation; if not prohibited by the vehicle

text: For the vehicle-based overcharge test of externally chargeable vehicles, the vehicle inlet for normal use, if it exists, shall be used for connecting the external electricity supply equipment, and the charge control communication of the equipment shall be altered or disabled to allow the specified charging.
condition: externally chargeable vehicles, charge by external electricity supply

text: The REESS shall be charged by the external electricity supply equipment with the maximum charge current specified by the manufacturer, and charging shall be terminated when the vehicle's overcharge protection control terminates the REESS charge current.
condition: charge by external electricity supply (vehicle-based test)

text: Where the vehicle's overcharge protection control fails to operate or there is no such control, charging by external electricity supply shall be continued until the REESS temperature reaches 10 °C above its maximum operating temperature specified by the manufacturer.
condition: charge by external electricity supply (vehicle-based); control fails or absent

text: Where charge current is not terminated and the REESS temperature remains less than 10 °C above the maximum operating temperature, vehicle operation shall be terminated 12 hours after the start of charging by external electricity supply equipment.
condition: charge by external electricity supply (vehicle-based)

text: Immediately after termination of charging, one standard cycle as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 shall be conducted, with vehicle operation on a chassis dynamometer for discharging and with external electricity supply equipment for charging, if not prohibited by the vehicle.
condition: charge by external electricity supply (vehicle-based); if not prohibited by the vehicle

text: For charging via breakout harness, the trip current/voltage setting of the external charge-discharge equipment shall be at least 10 per cent higher than the current/voltage limit of the Tested-Device, and the REESS shall be charged by the external electricity power supply with the maximum charge current specified by the manufacturer.
condition: vehicle-based test with breakout harness information provided by the manufacturer

text: In the breakout harness charging procedure, charging shall be terminated when the vehicle's overcharge protection control terminates the REESS charge current; where the control fails or is absent, charging shall be continued until the REESS temperature is 10 °C above its maximum operating temperature specified by the manufacturer.
condition: charge by connecting breakout harness

text: Where charge current is not terminated and the REESS temperature remains less than 10 °C above the maximum operating temperature, vehicle operation shall be terminated 12 hours after the start of charging by external electricity supply equipment.
condition: charge by connecting breakout harness

text: Immediately after termination of charging via breakout harness, one standard cycle as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 (for a complete vehicle) shall be conducted, if not prohibited by the vehicle.
condition: charge by connecting breakout harness; if not prohibited by the vehicle

text: For the component-based overcharge test, the external charge/discharge equipment shall be connected to the main terminals of the REESS and the charge control limits of the test equipment shall be disabled.
condition: component-based test

text: In the component-based overcharge test, the REESS shall be charged with the maximum charge current specified by the manufacturer and charging shall be terminated when the REESS overcharge protection control terminates the REESS charge current.
condition: component-based test

text: Where the REESS overcharge protection control fails to operate or there is no such control, charging shall be continued until the REESS temperature reaches 10 °C above its maximum operating temperature specified by the manufacturer.
condition: component-based test; control fails or absent

text: Where charge current is not terminated and the REESS temperature remains less than 10 °C above the maximum operating temperature, charging shall be terminated 12 hours after the start of charging by external electricity supply equipment.
condition: component-based test

text: Immediately after termination of charging in the component-based test, one standard cycle as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 shall be conducted with external charge-discharge equipment, if not prohibited by the REESS.
condition: component-based test; if not prohibited by the REESS

text: The overcharge protection test shall end with an observation period of 1 hour at the ambient temperature conditions of the test environment.
The over-discharge protection test shall be conducted, under standard operating conditions, either with a complete vehicle or with the complete REESS.
Ancillary systems may be omitted from the over-discharge Tested-Device and a modified Tested-Device may be used only provided they do not influence the test results.
The over-discharge protection test shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 20 ± 10 °C or at higher temperature if requested by the manufacturer.

For the over-discharge test, the SOC of the REESS shall be adjusted at the low level, but within normal operating range, by normal operation recommended by the manufacturer; accurate adjustment is not required as long as normal operation of the REESS is enabled.

For vehicle-based over-discharge test of vehicles with on-board energy conversion systems, the electrical energy from such systems shall be reduced, e.g. by adjusting the fuel level to nearly empty but enough for the vehicle to enter active driving possible mode.
condition: vehicle-based test of vehicles with on-board energy conversion systems

text: At the beginning of the over-discharge test, all protection devices which would affect the function of the Tested-Device and which are relevant for the outcome of the test shall be operational.
The procedure for discharging the REESS for the vehicle-based over-discharge test shall be in accordance with paragraphs 3.2.1. and 3.2.2.
condition: vehicle-based test

text: Alternatively, the discharging procedure for the vehicle-based over-discharge test shall be in accordance with paragraph 3.2.3.; for the component-based test it shall be in accordance with paragraph 3.2.4.

For discharge by vehicle driving operation, the vehicle shall be driven on a chassis dynamometer in active driving possible mode with an operation delivering as constant discharging power as reasonably achievable, determined if necessary through consultation with the manufacturer.
condition: discharge by vehicle driving operation

text: The vehicle operation on the chassis dynamometer shall be terminated when the vehicle's over-discharge protection control terminates REESS discharge current or the REESS temperature is stabilized such that it varies by a gradient of less than 4 °C through 2 hours.
condition: discharge by vehicle driving operation

text: Where an over-discharge protection control fails to operate or there is no such control, discharging shall be continued until the REESS is discharged to 25 per cent of its nominal voltage level.
condition: discharge by vehicle driving operation; control fails or absent

text: Immediately after termination of discharging, one standard charge followed by a standard discharge as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 shall be conducted if not prohibited by the vehicle.
condition: discharge by vehicle driving operation; if not prohibited by the vehicle

text: For discharge by auxiliary electrical equipment, the vehicle shall be switched into a stationary operation mode allowing consumption of REESS energy by auxiliary electrical equipment, determined if necessary through consultation with the manufacturer.
condition: discharge by auxiliary electrical equipment (vehicle-based)

text: The REESS shall be discharged by operation of electrical equipment (air-conditioning, heating, lighting, audio-visual equipment, etc.), and operation shall be terminated when the vehicle's over-discharge protection control terminates REESS discharge current or the REESS temperature varies by a gradient of less than 4 °C through 2 hours.
condition: discharge by auxiliary electrical equipment (vehicle-based)

text: Where an over-discharge protection control fails to operate or there is no such control, discharging by auxiliary equipment shall be continued until the REESS is discharged to 25 per cent of its nominal voltage level.
condition: discharge by auxiliary electrical equipment; control fails or absent

text: Immediately after termination of discharging by auxiliary equipment, one standard charge followed by a standard discharge as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 shall be conducted if not prohibited by the vehicle.
condition: discharge by auxiliary electrical equipment; if not prohibited by the vehicle

text: For discharge using a discharge resistor, the breakout harness shall be connected as specified by the manufacturer, the vehicle placed in active driving possible mode, and the REESS discharged through a discharge resistor at a discharge rate under normal operating conditions in accordance with manufacturer information (a 1 kW resistor may be used).
condition: vehicle-based test with breakout harness information provided by the manufacturer

text: The discharge resistor test shall be terminated when the vehicle's over-discharge protection control terminates REESS discharge current or the REESS temperature varies by a gradient of less than 4 °C through 2 hours; where an automatic discharge interrupt function fails or is absent, discharging shall continue until the REESS is discharged to 25 per cent of its nominal voltage level.
condition: discharge using discharge resistor

text: Immediately after termination of discharging via discharge resistor, one standard charge followed by a standard discharge as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 shall be conducted if not prohibited by the vehicle.
condition: discharge using discharge resistor; if not prohibited by the vehicle

text: For the component-based over-discharge test, all relevant main contactors shall be closed and the external charge-discharge equipment connected to the main terminals of the Tested-Device; discharge shall be performed with a stable current within the normal operating range specified by the manufacturer.
condition: component-based test

text: Discharging shall be continued until the Tested-Device terminates REESS discharge current or its temperature varies by a gradient of less than 4 °C through 2 hours; where an automatic interrupt function fails or is absent, discharging shall continue until the Tested-Device is discharged to 25 per cent of its nominal voltage level.
condition: component-based test

text: Immediately after termination of discharging in the component-based test, one standard charge followed by a standard discharge as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 shall be conducted if not inhibited by the Tested-Device.
condition: component-based test; if not inhibited by the Tested-Device

text: The over-discharge protection test shall end with an observation period of 1 h at the ambient temperature conditions of the test environment.
Where no specific protection measures are necessary to prevent the REESS from reaching an unsafe state due to internal over-temperature, this safe operation must be demonstrated.
condition: REESS without specific over-temperature protection measures

text: The over-temperature protection test shall be conducted with a complete REESS according to paragraphs 3. and 4. or with a complete vehicle according to paragraphs 5. and 6.
Ancillary systems may be omitted from the over-temperature Tested-Device and a modified Tested-Device may be used only provided they do not influence the test results.
condition: test using a complete REESS

text: Where a REESS is fitted with a cooling function and remains functional in delivering its normal power without the cooling system operational, the cooling system shall be deactivated for the over-temperature test.
condition: test using a complete REESS; REESS with cooling function functional without cooling

text: The temperature of the Tested-Device shall be continuously measured inside the casing in the proximity of the cells during the over-temperature test; the on-board sensor, if existing, may be used with compatible tools.
condition: test using a complete REESS

text: The REESS shall be placed in a convective oven or climatic chamber and, if necessary, connected to the rest of the vehicle control system with extended cables.
condition: test using a complete REESS

text: At the beginning of the over-temperature test, all protection devices which affect the function of the Tested-Device and are relevant to the outcome of the test shall be operational, except for any cooling deactivation per paragraph 3.2.
condition: test using a complete REESS

text: The Tested-Device shall be continuously charged and discharged by external charge/discharge equipment with a current that increases cell temperature as rapidly as possible within the range of normal operation defined by the manufacturer until the end of the test; alternatively by vehicle driving operations on a chassis dynamometer determined through consultation with the manufacturer.
condition: test using a complete REESS

text: The chamber or oven temperature shall be gradually increased from 20 ± 10 °C (or higher if requested by the manufacturer) to the temperature determined per paragraph 4.3.1. or 4.3.2., and then maintained at or above this temperature until the end of the test.
condition: test using a complete REESS

text: Where the REESS is equipped with protective measures against internal overheating, the chamber temperature shall be increased to the manufacturer-defined operational temperature threshold for such protective measures.
condition: REESS equipped with protective measures against internal overheating

text: Where the REESS is not equipped with specific measures against internal over-heating, the chamber temperature shall be increased to the maximum operational temperature specified by the manufacturer.
condition: REESS without specific measures against internal over-heating

text: The complete-REESS over-temperature test shall end when the Tested-Device inhibits and/or limits charge and/or discharge to prevent the temperature increase, or its temperature varies by a gradient of less than 4 °C through 2 hours, or any failure of the acceptance criteria of paragraph 6.9.2.1. occurs.
condition: test using a complete REESS

text: For a vehicle-based over-temperature test, based on manufacturer information, the cooling system of a REESS fitted with a cooling function shall be disabled, or in a state of significantly reduced operation for a REESS that will not operate with the cooling system disabled.
condition: test using a complete vehicle; REESS fitted with cooling function

text: In the vehicle-based over-temperature test, the REESS temperature shall be continuously measured inside the casing in the proximity of the cells using on-board sensors and compatible tools according to manufacturer information.
condition: test using a complete vehicle

text: The vehicle shall be placed in a climate control chamber set to a temperature between 40 °C to 45 °C for at least 6 hours.
condition: test using a complete vehicle

text: In the over-temperature test using a complete vehicle, the vehicle shall be continuously charged and discharged in a manner that will increase the temperature of REESS cells as rapidly as possible within the range of normal operation as defined by the manufacturer until the end of the test.
condition: test conducted using a complete vehicle

text: The charge and discharge shall be conducted by vehicle driving operations on a chassis dynamometer, where the driving operation shall be determined through consultation with the manufacturer.
condition: test conducted using a complete vehicle

text: For a vehicle that can be charged by an external power supply, the charging may be conducted using an external power supply if more rapid temperature increase is expected.
condition: vehicle can be charged by an external power supply

text: The vehicle-based over-temperature test shall end when one of the following is observed: (a) the vehicle terminates the charge and/or discharge; (b) the REESS temperature is stabilized such that the temperature varies by a gradient of less than 4 °C through 2 hours; (c) any failure of the acceptance criteria of paragraph 6.9.2.1.; (d) three hours elapse from the start of the charge/discharge cycles.
condition: test conducted using a complete vehicle

text: The overcurrent protection test shall be conducted at an ambient temperature of 20 ± 10 °C.

For the overcurrent test, the SOC of the REESS shall be adjusted around the middle of the normal operating range by normal operation recommended by the manufacturer such as driving the vehicle or using an external charger; accurate adjustment is not required as long as normal operation of the REESS is enabled.

The overcurrent level (assuming failure of external DC electricity supply equipment) and maximum voltage (within normal range) that can be applied shall be determined, if necessary, through consultation with the manufacturer.
The overcurrent test shall be conducted in accordance with paragraph 4. or paragraph 5. of Annex 9J, as applicable, and in accordance with manufacturer information.

In the vehicle-based overcurrent test, the DC charging vehicle inlet shall be used for connecting the external DC electricity supply equipment, with the charge control communication of the external equipment altered or disabled to allow the overcurrent level determined through consultation with the manufacturer.
condition: vehicle-based test for vehicles capable of charging by DC external electricity supply

text: Charging of the REESS by the external DC electricity supply equipment shall be initiated to achieve the highest normal charge current specified by the manufacturer, then increased over 5 seconds to the determined overcurrent level and continued at this overcurrent level.
condition: vehicle-based test for vehicles capable of charging by DC external electricity supply

text: The charging shall be terminated when the vehicle's overcurrent protection terminates the REESS charge current or the REESS temperature is stabilized such that the temperature varies by a gradient of less than 4 °C through 2 hours.
condition: vehicle-based test for vehicles capable of charging by DC external electricity supply

text: Immediately after the termination of charging, one standard cycle as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 shall be conducted, if it is not prohibited by the vehicle.
condition: vehicle-based test for vehicles capable of charging by DC external electricity supply

text: In the breakout harness overcurrent test, the breakout harness shall be connected to the vehicle or REESS as specified by the manufacturer, and the external electricity supply equipment with the overcurrent supply connected to it, initiating charging to the highest normal charge current specified by the manufacturer.
