condition: REESS for vehicles capable of DC external charging where the manufacturer provides breakout harness connection information

text: The charge current shall be increased over 5 seconds from the highest normal charge current to the determined overcurrent level and charging continued at this overcurrent level.
condition: test using breakout harness

text: The charging shall be terminated when the vehicle's overcurrent protection terminates charging or the Tested-Device temperature is stabilized such that the temperature varies by a gradient of less than 4 °C through 2 hours.
condition: test using breakout harness

text: Immediately after the termination of charging, one standard cycle as described in Annex 9, Appendix 1 shall be conducted, if it is not prohibited by the vehicle.
condition: test using breakout harness

text: The overcurrent test shall end with an observation period of 1 hour at the ambient temperature conditions of the test environment.

The thermal propagation test shall be conducted either with a complete vehicle or using the complete REESS or REESS subsystem(s) at the discretion of the manufacturer in agreement with the Technical Service.

If the manufacturer chooses to test with REESS subsystem(s), the manufacturer shall demonstrate that the test result can reasonably represent the performance of the complete REESS with respect to its safety performance under the same conditions.
condition: test with REESS subsystem(s)

text: For a test using REESS or REESS subsystem, the parts of the vehicle relevant for the test shall be installed to the Tested-Device in case phenomena rendering the test non-representative of REESS installed in a vehicle are expected.
condition: component-based test where non-representative phenomena are expected

text: In case of outdoor thermal propagation testing there shall be no direct exposure of the vehicle/Tested-Device to precipitation for the duration of the test.
condition: outdoor testing

text: Immediately before the test, the wind speed shall be measured at a location no more than 5 m from the Tested-Device and the average wind speed over 10 min shall be less than 7.8 m/s.
It shall be ensured that the results are not affected by gusts of wind; gusts shall not exceed 10 m/s when measured over a period of 20 s.
The test set-up shall consider the impact of features such as shielding screens or walls which may create excessive funnelling effects during the test.
Required modifications of the Tested-Device shall be kept to a minimum compared to the original unmodified Tested-Device.

Any modifications of REESS components, such as mechanical and thermal barriers, cooling plates/channels, electrical connections and cell-to-cell spacing, shall be documented with justification as to why such changes will not result in a significant change in performance.
It shall be confirmed that the original sealing capability of the REESS is not compromised by instrumentation and that any venting shall be through pre-existing seals.

All components and features required for the functioning of the Tested-Device and safety related features (e.g. cell connecting busbars, tab welding, connection and functionality of the management system, isolation resistance) shall be maintained and not compromised.
For the vehicle-level thermal propagation test, all windows, roof and doors are closed.
condition: vehicle-level test

text: At the beginning of the test, the State of Charge shall be adjusted according to the procedure described in Annex 9 - Appendix 1.

At the beginning of the test and for as long as possible during the test, all necessary functions of the Tested-Device shall be operational, and the Tested-Device shall be representative of the REESS installed in a vehicle that is stationary and in active-driving possible mode.

The defined thermal management/safety strategy and the battery management system used in the REESS shall be fully operational; the native thermal management strategy (if installed) and other relevant management systems necessary for the test shall be operational for as long as possible during the test.

Immediately before turning on the initiation device, the temperature of the cells in the Tested-Device shall be maintained between 18 °C and the maximum operating temperature defined by the manufacturer.

The selection of the initiation cell shall consider the number of adjacent cells, cell packaging, the distance between cells in proximity to the potential initiation cell, and the practicality of initiation.
A representative case for the initiation cell shall be determined by the Technical Service, in consultation with the manufacturer, on the basis of documentation provided by the manufacturer.
The installation of test equipment shall not compromise the functionality of the REESS relevant to the safety performance and shall minimize modification to thermal insulators and structure.
The installation of test equipment shall not disable or affect the functionality of the battery management systems.
The installation of test equipment shall not change pack gas flow direction and permeability, both internal and exit paths.

The selected initiation cell shall represent severe conditions for the generation of potentially hazardous conditions in the event of a thermal runaway, i.e. a high level of heat transfer to at least one adjacent cell, subjection to heat sink(s) and non-productive thermal pathway(s), or any other condition or location known by the manufacturer which could potentially lead to a hazardous condition.
All data measurement systems shall be referenced to the same starting time.
The identification of the test method, including the trigger method, and a description of the test set-up shall be recorded.
The test conditions (e.g. environmental conditions, SoC and other pre-conditioning parameters) shall be recorded.
The temperature of the initiation cell shall be recorded during the test and observation period, ensuring that the trigger device or test instrumentation does not influence the measurement.
The voltage of the initiation cell during the thermal runaway triggering procedure shall be recorded.
The temperature of one adjacent cell shall be recorded.
Video and audio recording, including time stamps of observable events (e.g. initiation cell thermal runaway and venting, thermal propagation, smoke, fire or flame, explosion), shall be recorded.
The condition of the Tested-Device at the end of the test, supported by video or photographs (before and after test), shall be recorded.

For a vehicle-level test, the time stamp of warning indications or alarms to occupants shall be recorded; for a REESS or REESS subsystem test, the time stamp of the signal to trigger the warning indications shall be recorded.

Thermal runaway of the initiation cell shall be detected when either (a) the measured voltage drop exceeds 25 per cent of the initial voltage for at least 1 second and dT/dt ≥ 1 °C/s for at least 3 consecutive seconds, or (b) the measured temperature exceeds the maximum operating temperature defined by the manufacturer and dT/dt ≥ 1 °C/s for at least 3 consecutive seconds.

The trigger method shall not affect the adjacent cell(s); if localized rapid external heating, localized internal heating or laser-based trigger methods are used, the temperature of the adjacent cell(s) shall not exceed the maximum operating temperature defined by the manufacturer before thermal runaway of the initiation cell is detected.
Appropriate methods may be used to isolate the adjacent cell(s) only provided that the original functionality of the REESS is not impeded.

The feed-through connections for the heating element and measuring sensors must provide greater sealing integrity than the other REESS connectors, and should only modify the REESS by allowing the necessary electrical and thermocouple connections.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: The selected heating element shall not be in direct contact with any surface of the components in the Tested-Device other than the initiation cell.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: A contact pressure for the heating element on the initiation cell shall be maintained during the test to ensure contact and optimal heat transfer.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: For vehicle-based tests, the vehicle response shall not be influenced by the external heater trigger method in the REESS.
condition: vehicle-based test with localized rapid external heater

text: A temperature sensor shall be placed on the surface of the heating element and affixed with high-temperature resistant and electrically insulating tape for power regulation of the heater.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: The heater shall not apply so much power that there is a premature heating element failure or a side wall failure of the initiation cell prior to thermal runaway.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: The heating device shall be a resistive heating element, or other suitable heating device/technology capable of delivering the target parameters of Table 1.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: Heater device material target: a suitable resistive heating material, e.g. nickel-chrome, with an isolating barrier.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: Heater element thickness target: < 5 mm.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: Heater element area target: as small as possible, but no larger than 20 per cent of the surface area of the targeted face of the initiation cell.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: Heater heating rate target: ≥ 15 °C/s, measured by an external thermocouple placed on top of the heating element installed in the pack.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: Heater maximum temperature target: at least 100 °C larger than the maximum operating temperature; the heater shall maintain integrity.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: Heater control method target: thermostatic closed loop.
condition: localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: The general conditions in Annex 9K, paragraph 3 shall be satisfied when the external heater method is implemented with the vehicle.
condition: vehicle-based test with localized rapid external heater

text: The REESS and the vehicle shall be instrumented and the vehicle placed in active-driving possible mode, making sure that the cooling and communication system operate as intended.
condition: vehicle-based test with localized rapid external heater

text: Data recording shall be started to determine thermal runaway and/or thermal propagation, and it shall be verified that fault codes or failures relevant for the outcome of the test are not in the system.
condition: vehicle-based test with localized rapid external heater

text: The heater shall be switched off after a total energy input to the heater reaches 20 per cent of initiation cell energy.
condition: vehicle-based test with localized rapid external heater

text: If the heater is switched off at 20 per cent energy input and thermal runaway has not occurred in the initiation cell during the observation period of 1 hour after the opening of the heater relay, the REESS type is considered to comply.
condition: vehicle-based test with localized rapid external heater

text: The test ends when: (i) initiation is stopped followed by an observation period of 1 hour; or (ii) at least 5 minutes elapse after activation of the warning indication, if thermal propagation is observed; or (iii) if thermal runaway occurred in the initiation cell without thermal propagation, after an observation period of 2 hours after confirmation of thermal runaway.
condition: vehicle-based test with localized rapid external heater

text: For the component-based thermal propagation test with a localized rapid external heater, the general conditions in Annex 9K, paragraph 3 shall be satisfied when the method is implemented on the REESS or REESS subsystem.
condition: component-based test using the localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: The REESS or REESS subsystem shall be instrumented and prepared such that it represents the situation when installed in the vehicle with the system in active-driving possible mode, and the thermal management and communication system shall operate as intended.
condition: component-based test using the localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: Recording of the data necessary to determine if thermal runaway and/or thermal propagation occur shall be started, and it shall be verified that fault codes or failures relevant for the outcome of the test are not in the system.
condition: component-based test using the localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: The heater shall be switched off immediately when thermal runaway is confirmed or after total energy input to the heater reaches 20 per cent of initiation cell electric energy.
condition: component-based test using the localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: If the heater has been switched off after 20 per cent energy input but thermal runaway has not occurred in the initiation cell during the observation period of 1 hour after the opening of the heater relay, the REESS type is considered to comply.
condition: component-based test using the localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: The test ends when: (i) initiation is stopped followed by an observation period of 1 hour; or (ii) at least 5 minutes elapse after the signal to activate the warning indication, if thermal propagation is observed; or (iii) if thermal runaway occurred in the initiation cell but no thermal propagation ensued, an observation period of 2 hours after confirmation of thermal runaway is applied.
condition: component-based test using the localized rapid external heater trigger method

text: With the internal heater trigger method, the temperature of the adjacent cell(s), prior to thermal runaway in the initiation cell, shall remain below the maximum operating temperature.
condition: internal heater trigger method (Annex 9K Appendix 2)

text: The internal heating device shall be a resistive heating element, or other suitable heating device/technology capable of delivering the target parameters of Table 1.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: The resistance, power and duration of the internal heater shall be adjusted according to the electrochemistry and the size of the cell.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: Internal heating element material: a suitable resistive heating material with an insulating barrier, e.g. copper or tungsten.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: Internal heating element thickness: ≤ 0.5 mm.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: Internal heating element area: 225 - 500 mm2.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: Internal heater power: 150~700 W.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: The internal heater shall be inserted in the connected electrode stack or jellyroll of the initiation cell before cell sealing.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: One or two hole(s) are drilled into the initiation cell cover to allow the electrical feedthrough of the heater from inside the cell to the outside.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: The separators and electrodes of the initiation cell are unrolled to insert the heater.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: The heater is located on the last wrap of electrode, between the outermost negative and positive electrodes of the cell; unrolling a larger part of the jelly roll shall be avoided, and an outer stack is used in case of stacked layers.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: The jelly roll is wound with the heater inside.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: All wires used in the REESS or REESS subsystem shall be electrically isolated.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: The initiation cell shall be assembled according to standard manufacturing processes ensuring no electrolyte or gases can leak out through the space between the wire strand and the wire insulator.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: The strength of the resin seal of the heater supply shall be greater than any installed vent of the cell.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: After the resin is completely dry, a helium test shall be carried out to check the sealing before filling the cell with electrolyte.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: The initiation cell shall be assembled inside the REESS or REESS subsystem, which may be modified so that the electrical feedthrough of the heater can come out of the cell block.
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: The feedthrough installation of the heating element and measuring sensors should only modify the REESS (or REESS subsystem) by permitting necessary electrical and thermocouple connections, and these connections shall provide greater seal integrity than the other connectors in the REESS (or REESS subsystem).
condition: internal heater trigger method

text: For a vehicle level test, the REESS shall be mounted on the vehicle according to the manufacturer's specifications.
condition: internal heater trigger method, vehicle level test

text: For the vehicle-based test with the internal heater, the general conditions in Annex 9K, paragraph 3 shall be satisfied.
condition: vehicle-based test using the internal heater trigger method

text: The REESS and vehicle shall be instrumented, the vehicle placed in active-driving possible mode, and the cooling and communication system shall operate as intended.
condition: vehicle-based test using the internal heater trigger method

text: Data recording to determine thermal runaway and/or thermal propagation shall be started, and it shall be verified that fault codes or failures relevant for the outcome of the test are not in the system.
condition: vehicle-based test using the internal heater trigger method

text: The internal heater shall be switched off immediately when thermal runaway is confirmed or after a total energy input to the heater reaches 20 % of initiation cell electric energy.
condition: vehicle-based test using the internal heater trigger method

text: If no thermal runaway has occurred in the initiation cell during the observation period of 1 hour after the opening of the heater relay, the REESS type is considered to comply.
condition: vehicle-based test using the internal heater trigger method

text: The test ends when: (i) initiation is stopped followed by an observation period of 1 hour; or (ii) at least 5 minutes elapse after activation of the warning indication, if thermal propagation is observed; or (iii) if thermal runaway occurred but no thermal propagation ensued, an observation period of 2 hours after confirmation of thermal runaway is applied.
condition: vehicle-based test using the internal heater trigger method

text: For the component-based test with the internal heater, the general conditions in Annex 9K, paragraph 3 shall be satisfied, and the REESS or REESS subsystem shall be prepared to represent installation in the vehicle in active-driving possible mode with thermal management and communication system operating as intended.
condition: component-based test using the internal heater trigger method

text: Data recording shall be started and it shall be verified that no relevant fault codes or failures are in the system; the internal heater shall be switched off immediately when thermal runaway is confirmed or after total energy input reaches 20 % of initiation cell electric energy.
condition: component-based test using the internal heater trigger method

text: If no thermal runaway occurs in the initiation cell during 1 hour observation after opening of the heater relay the REESS type is considered to comply; the test ends after 1 hour observation following stopped initiation, at least 5 minutes after the signal to activate the warning indication if thermal propagation is observed, or 2 hours after confirmation of thermal runaway if no propagation ensued.
condition: component-based test using the internal heater trigger method

text: If the REESS is enclosed in a housing, a penetrating hole may be made in the housing to insert the nail; a device such as a gas tight sleeve for the nail preventing venting gas from leaking out from the nail hole should be applied, if necessary.
condition: nail penetration trigger method

text: The nail penetrating position and direction are selected where causing a thermal runaway in the initiation cell is possible (e.g. perpendicular to electrode layer).
condition: nail penetration trigger method

text: The details of the nail trigger method including appropriate parameters recommended by the manufacturer in accordance with paragraph 6.15.3.1.(f) shall be respected subject to the agreement of the Technical Service.
condition: nail penetration trigger method

text: Nail material: steel.
condition: nail penetration trigger method, nail chosen from Table 1

text: Nail diameter: 3 to 8 mm.
condition: nail penetration trigger method, nail chosen from Table 1

text: Nail angle of tip: 20 to 60°.
condition: nail penetration trigger method, nail chosen from Table 1

text: Nail penetrating speed: 0.1 to 1 mm/s.
condition: nail penetration trigger method, nail chosen from Table 1

text: For the vehicle-based nail penetration test, the general conditions in Annex 9K, paragraph 3 shall be satisfied; the REESS shall be instrumented, all thermal management and high voltage lines connected, and the REESS reinstalled into the vehicle.
condition: vehicle-based test using nail penetration

text: Data recording shall be started, absence of relevant fault codes or failures verified, and the nail shape, diameter and penetrating speed selected according to paragraph 2.(iv).
condition: vehicle-based test using nail penetration

text: The nail shall be stopped and remain inside the initiation cell when thermal runaway is confirmed or the nail has penetrated both the front and back side of the cell.
condition: vehicle-based test using nail penetration

text: The nail penetration vehicle-based test ends after 1 hour observation following stopped initiation, at least 5 minutes after activation of the warning indication if thermal propagation is observed, or 2 hours after confirmation of thermal runaway if no thermal propagation ensued.
condition: vehicle-based test using nail penetration

text: For the component-based nail penetration test, the general conditions in Annex 9K, paragraph 3 shall be satisfied and the REESS or REESS subsystem prepared to represent installation in the vehicle in active-driving possible mode with thermal management and communication system operating as intended.
condition: component-based test using nail penetration

text: Data recording shall be started, absence of relevant fault codes verified, nail parameters selected per paragraph 2.(iv), and the nail stopped and left inside the initiation cell when thermal runaway is confirmed or the nail has penetrated both front and back side of the cell.
condition: component-based test using nail penetration

text: The component-based nail penetration test ends after 1 hour observation following stopped initiation, at least 5 minutes after the signal to activate the warning indication if thermal propagation is observed, or 2 hours after confirmation of thermal runaway if no thermal propagation ensued.
condition: component-based test using nail penetration

text: Before conducting the laser-based trigger test, the laser beam path shall be secured so that the laser beam reaches a predetermined position on the initiation cell surface.
condition: laser-based trigger method

text: The laser type may be chosen from material process lasers such as used for cutting, welding or hardening (e.g. CO2, YAG, semiconductor, disk or fibre laser).
condition: laser-based trigger method

text: For the vehicle-based laser test, the general conditions in Annex 9K, paragraph 3 shall be satisfied; the REESS shall be instrumented, thermal management and high voltage lines connected and the REESS reinstalled into the vehicle; data recording started and absence of relevant fault codes verified.
condition: vehicle-based test using laser-based trigger

text: The laser beam path shall be secured to reach the initiation cell surface, the laser irradiation program set and confirmed, and the initiation cell irradiated at the determined point.
condition: vehicle-based test using laser-based trigger

text: The laser irradiation program shall be stopped when thermal runaway is confirmed or after a total energy input from the laser reaches 20 per cent of the initiation cell energy.
condition: vehicle-based test using laser-based trigger

text: If no thermal runaway occurs in the initiation cell during 1 hour observation after laser switch off the REESS type is considered to comply; the test ends after 1 hour observation following stopped initiation, 5 minutes after activation of the warning indication if thermal propagation is observed, or 2 hours after confirmation of thermal runaway if no propagation ensued.
condition: vehicle-based test using laser-based trigger

text: For the component-based laser test, the general conditions in Annex 9K, paragraph 3 shall be satisfied and the REESS or REESS subsystem prepared to represent installation in the vehicle in active-driving possible mode with thermal management and communication system operating as intended; data recording started and absence of relevant fault codes verified.
condition: component-based test using laser-based trigger

text: The laser beam path shall be secured, the irradiation program set and confirmed, the initiation cell irradiated at the determined point, and irradiation stopped when thermal runaway is confirmed or after total laser energy input reaches 20 per cent of the initiation cell energy.
condition: component-based test using laser-based trigger

text: If thermal runaway does not occur in the initiation cell during 1 hour observation after laser switch off the REESS type is considered to comply; the test ends after 1 hour observation following stopped initiation, 5 minutes after the signal to activate the warning indication if thermal propagation is observed, or 2 hours after confirmation of thermal runaway if no propagation ensued.
condition: component-based test using laser-based trigger
